interactions.mechanism: Shootout skill only matters when the match reaches penalties, so its weight in the Method price is the product of P(draw at 90) and P(ET draw); in a lopsided tie that product is under 6% and skill is negligible.

interactions.mechanism: Home advantage multiplies the intensity ratio, so in a neutral-venue final it disappears and the favourite's first-scorer odds fall by several percentage points relative to the same pairing at home.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit first-scorer indicator with home and neutral flags.

interactions.mechanism: A depleted favourite (missing starters) has a lower win-in-90 but a smaller drop in ET win, because ET advantage depends on bench depth and fitness more than on the starting XI; the effect on the tree is node-dependent.

contract.settlement_definition: Spread series: YES when the named team wins the regulation match (90 minutes plus stoppage, extra time and penalties excluded) by strictly more than the x.5 strike, e.g. 'wins by more than 2.5 goals' means a margin of 3 or more; because strikes are half-goals there is no push. Correct-score series: each market is a single scoreline for a named winner ('Switzerland wins 5-2'), settled on the 90-minute final score; the sampled texts do not show the draw or 'any other score' rungs. Cancelled matches or those moved beyond 48 hours resolve to a fair price in the generic game rules (visible in sibling game series). Own goals count in the score.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: The margin is measured at the end of regulation so an extra-time win by two does not settle the spread; Coupe de France ties between divisions are full of 90-minute draws that go to ET.

rules_evidence.quote: If PSG wins by more than 5.5 goals in the PSG vs Le Havre professional French Women's Première Ligue
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread strikes extend to 5.5 in lopsided women's league fixtures; the margin tail beyond five goals is a mismatch event, not Poisson noise.

rules_evidence.quote: If Switzerland wins 5-2 in the Switzerland vs North Macedonia professional UEFA Nations League soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-score rungs are one specific scoreline for a specific winner, so a 7-goal match is a single rung and the ladder sums to one over all scorelines.

rules_evidence.quote: If UD Maracena wins 5-2 in the UD Maracena vs UE Tavernes professional Copa del Rey soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Copa del Rey first rounds pair amateur sides with professional ones; very high exact scores are live rungs and sampled markets even for 5-2.

variants_and_edge_cases: Spread strikes are x.5 'wins by more than' with strike_type greater (e.g. KXLALIGA2SPREAD 3.5): P(margin>=4) is a deep-tail event for most pairings, so the tail of goal difference and mismatch magnitude (cup ties across divisions) dominate rather than lambda differences.

Exact score requires a correct joint distribution of each team's count: a 'wins 5-2' rung needs the loser to score 2, which is very sensitive to the loser's conversion in a chasing game; the ladder across hundreds of rungs must be a proper joint distribution (monotone and summing to one).

Cup ties that need a winner go to ET and penalties but the contract is settled at 90 minutes, so a team that leads 1-0 and concedes a 94th-minute equaliser has no ET effect; abandonment inside the match is not in the sampled text.

177 live series, only 7 with rules text; the others (KXLIGAEXPSPREAD, KXENGNLSPREAD, KXALLSVENSKANSPREAD ...) are TITLE_ONLY; the hybrid 'wins by more than N' strikes also exist for first-half spreads, which are in first_half_and_period.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report final score after regulation including stoppage time, own goals credited to the beneficiary; extra time and shootout results explicitly not used.

mechanism.summary: A handicap or exact score settles on the regulation goal difference or scoreline, so the object is the joint distribution of two team goal counts. The mean gap comes from team strengths (with a bridge between divisions for cup mismatches) and from the confirmed lineup; the favourite's rotation in mismatch games is a major discrete driver. The tail of the margin differs from independent Poisson: leaders ease off after a large lead and underdogs can collapse, and the base rate of mismatches depends on the league's competitive balance. Exact-score rungs depend on cell-level dependence in low scores and on the trailing side's scoring while chasing. The ladders are nested (spreads) or a partition (scores), settled at 90 minutes.

stages.name: Strength gap between the two teams
stages.description: A handicap and a correct score first require the full distribution of the strength gap: league-adjusted attack/defence strengths for both teams, venue, and a bridge between divisions when cup sides come from different tiers. Rating error for the weaker side is large in cups (small samples, no common opponents), so the mismatch size is itself uncertain.
stages.distribution: Log-normal-ish posterior of attack and defence per team; the gap between divisions has sd of about 0.3-0.5 log-goals when linked only by sparse cup results.

stages.name: Lineup and rotation of the favourite
stages.description: In cups and congested weeks big clubs rotate heavily against small clubs, which reduces the favourite's lambda by 15-30% and changes who plays up front; the confirmed XI shifts the margin distribution far more than the opponent does. Depth of the favourite's bench determines how large the drop is.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup states (full strength / rotated / reserves) with probabilities that depend on stakes; lambda scale shifts by regime.

stages.name: Goal-difference distribution and its tail
stages.description: Given the two lambdas the margin is a Skellam-like difference, but real blowouts have a different tail: after a 3-0 lead the favourite eases off (lowering its lambda), while a collapsing underdog (red card, tactical disorganisation) concedes in bunches. The league's competitive balance sets how often mismatches occur and how fat the tail of margins is.
stages.distribution: Difference of correlated overdispersed counts; the tail beyond margin 4 is thicker than Skellam in lopsided leagues, thinner after garbage time sets in.

stages.name: Low and mid scoreline structure for exact scores
stages.description: Exact-score rungs depend on the joint distribution cell by cell: the 0-0, 1-0, 1-1 cells use Dixon-Coles dependence, and cells like 3-1, 2-2 depend on the two teams' high-count behaviour; the loser's scoring chance when trailing (chasing) matters for 4-2 vs 4-0.
stages.distribution: Joint pmf over scorelines with heavy mass at 1-0, 1-1, 2-1; each cell probability below 15% so rung prices are small and noise-sensitive.

stages.name: Ladder consistency and settlement
stages.description: Spread strikes form a nested monotone ladder (P(margin>3.5) <= P(margin>2.5)) and correct-score rungs form a partition; regulation-only settlement and the 'winner' conditional in each rung determine mapping. Cancellation and fair-price rules apply.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; constraint structure rather than randomness.

soc.cross_tier_strength_link.label: Cross-division bridge rating for cup mismatches
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.mechanism: Estimated strength difference between divisions or leagues from cup ties and European fixtures.
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.rationale: In Coupe de France, Copa del Rey or FA Cup rounds there are no common opponents; ratings estimated within leagues are on different scales, and the bridge parameter drives the expected margin and so the spread ladder.
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.measurement: Fit a joint rating model across divisions/leagues using all inter-division matches (cups, European club competitions, friendlies): rating_i = league_effect(L_i) + team_effect_i with a random-walk-on-season; league effect posterior with sd; update weekly; shrink team effects to division mean with k=12 matches; as-of = prior to kickoff.
soc.cross_tier_strength_link.why: Large cup mismatches are the main source of high spread and exact-score rungs and need explicit division bridging.

soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.label: Favourite's rotation intensity in mismatch fixtures
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.mechanism: Predicted number and quality of changed starters for a big club facing a lower-ranked side.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.rationale: A rotated favourite loses 15-30% of attacking output but a full-strength one may win by five; the spread ladder swings between regimes, and the rotation is partly predictable from the cup, midweek schedule and manager history.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.measurement: Ordinal logit of starters changed (0, 1-3, 4-6, 7+) on: days since last match, days to next major match, competition type, rating gap, manager rotation propensity (past 30 matches); output expected lambda multiplier = sum_k P(k) * m_k, with m_k estimated by regressing xG on number of rotated starters (with player-quality weights); re-evaluate at lineup release.
soc.favourite_rotation_in_mismatch.why: Dominant spread driver in cup fixtures that no strength rating captures.

soc.blowout_tail_inflation.label: Empirical tail of goal difference relative to Skellam, by gap quantile
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.mechanism: Excess or deficit of large margins compared with the independent-Poisson prediction.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.rationale: At strikes 3.5-5.5 the model's tail fraction is wrong by tens of percent when game-state (garbage time, collapse) is ignored; calibrating on history is the only way to price the deep tail.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.measurement: Pool 10 seasons of matches; bin by pre-match expected goal difference; compute observed P(margin >= m) / model P(margin >= m) for m in {2,3,4,5} per league group; smoothed with isotonic regression and hierarchical shrinkage across leagues (k=100 matches per bin); output multiplicative tail correction factors.
soc.blowout_tail_inflation.why: Mismatch-driven spreads depend more on tail calibration than on mean strength.

soc.league_strength_dispersion.label: League competitive balance: sd of team strengths
soc.league_strength_dispersion.mechanism: Dispersion of ratings within a league-season.
soc.league_strength_dispersion.rationale: A league with one dominant club (Scotland, Women's Première Ligue, Turkish and Greek top halves) generates many 4+ goal margins compared with a balanced league; the base rate of mismatches differs by league and the model should reflect it.
soc.league_strength_dispersion.measurement: Per league-season: sd of team rating (attack-defence) from the ratings model, plus P(expected margin > 1.5) share of fixtures; compute rolling 3-season values with shrinkage to a global value (k=2 seasons).
soc.league_strength_dispersion.why: Calibrates base rates of lopsided games by league, where sampled spreads reach 5.5 goals.

soc.score_state.reason: Not pregame; calibrates damping and collapse in the tail.

contract.settlement_definition: Each match has three mutually exclusive binaries (home wins, away wins, 'Tie is the result'), settled on the score after 90 minutes plus stoppage time; extra time and penalties are explicitly excluded, so in cup ties a team that wins on penalties still leaves 'Tie' as the YES outcome. Matches cancelled or rescheduled to more than 48 hours away resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules rather than to No. The 3-way set sums to one. Also in the ledger bucket are same-event Spread and Total series (KXARGPREMDIVSPREAD, KXARGPREMDIVTOTAL) which are different contracts.

rules_evidence.establishes: Draw is its own contract; for the Premier League there is no extra time anyway, but a draw is a priced outcome, not a void or push.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Even in a continental knockout, the result is judged at the end of regulation, so draw probability at 90 is the object, not who advances.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over 48 hours away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement settlement is a fair-price void: a market holder is not hurt by weather postponements beyond 48 hours but a short delay under 48 hours leaves the contract live.

rules_evidence.establishes: Friendlies are listed with the same settlement as competitive league games, which creates a different data-generating process (rotation, substitution waves) under the same contract text.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Bolivian Premier Division at altitude settles identically to European games, so the altitude advantage enters through the goal process only.

variants_and_edge_cases: Three binaries per match must be coherent: P(home)+P(draw)+P(away)=1; each is its own series entry (e.g. KXMLSGAME ticker suffix -TIE vs team codes), so mispricing can sit in the draw leg alone.

Two-way 'winner' wording (match_winner_2way in the catalog family) is not in the sampled texts; the ledger has no live evidence that a no-draw version exists, so the 2-way target in the catalog is unverified.

Cup ties, club friendlies and Libertadores/Sudamericana knockouts mix incentives (aggregate state, rotation, substitution waves up to 6 players) under the same 90-minute settlement; two-leg aggregate position changes the draw rate without changing the contract.
Stoppage time is part of the window: late goals in 90+ minutes count, and 90+N length depends on VAR and substitution; abandonment mid-match (weather, crowd) is not covered in the sampled text.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report score at full time of regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage time) from the competition's governing body, which Kalshi's data provider mirrors; extra time and shootouts not used.

mechanism.summary: The 3-way result is the sign of the regulation goal difference, with the draw as a separate priced leg. Expected goal difference comes from adjusted team strengths and team-specific home advantage, then moves with the actual lineup (the part that was not predicted), rotation and stakes, fatigue and travel, and for specific leagues altitude. The draw probability depends on the total goal environment and on low-cell dependence, peaking when teams are balanced and totals are low; referee shocks and red cards add rare large effects. The contract settles on 90 minutes plus stoppage time with extra time and penalties excluded and a fair-price void for postponements, and friendlies and cups share the same settlement but different incentives.

stages.name: Team strength differential
stages.description: The expected goal difference comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths with decay and shrinkage, plus home advantage by team and league, and a preseason or promotion prior when evidence is thin. The rating gap, scaled by the competition's goal environment, sets the shape of win/draw/loss probabilities.
stages.distribution: Latent strengths are Bayesian posteriors with sd about 0.1-0.15 in log goal-rate; three-way outcome follows from a bivariate goal model.

stages.name: Who plays: lineup, rotation and surprise
stages.description: The market already prices the expected XI, so the informative quantity is the deviation of the actual lineup from the predicted one, together with suspensions, injuries to key players and manager rotation in congested weeks. A missing goalkeeper or playmaker is worth roughly 0.1-0.25 goals of expected goal difference.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup scenarios; effect on goal difference is heavy-tailed and sparse (most matches change little, some change a lot).

stages.name: Fatigue, travel and situational context
stages.description: Rest days, minutes load, travel and time-zone change, international-break returns and the stakes of the match (title or relegation leverage, dead rubbers, rivalry) shift effort and rotation; altitude and heat in parts of South America and CONCACAF alter the physiological advantage of the home side far beyond ordinary home advantage.
stages.distribution: Smaller effects (0.05-0.15 goals) except altitude which can be 0.3-0.5 goals; many correlated small shocks.

stages.name: Draw mass and low-scoring structure
stages.description: The draw is the most mispriced outcome: its probability depends on the total goal environment (lower totals raise draws), on the dependence between teams in low cells (Dixon-Coles) and on team-specific draw tendencies from style (low-block, cagey sides). Draw probability is about 26% on average, peaking when expected goal difference is near zero.
stages.distribution: Discrete 0-0/1-1 cell masses; draw rate is bounded in the 20-33% range for league games with a peak at balanced matches.

stages.name: Officiating and shocks
stages.description: Referee choices (penalties about 0.3 per match, red cards about 0.1) and VAR create sudden shifts in the match; a first-half red card changes the expected goal difference by about 0.5 goals. These are mostly unpredictable but have referee-level baselines.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete shocks with large effects; right skewed on goal difference.

stages.name: Settlement and market-type bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement is the 90-minute score; the contract boundary must be correctly implemented for cup ties, and the three outcome markets must be consistent. Friendlies and cups use different incentive structure but the same settlement; the market-derived odds are only a benchmark for validation.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the final regulation score; no randomness beyond the match.

soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.label: Deviation of the actual XI from the predicted XI
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.mechanism: Value difference between the lineup announced at about T-60 and the lineup forecast from the previous day.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.rationale: A model keyed on 'XI vs season-average' gives credit for information the market had hours earlier; the new information at lineup release is the surprise relative to the predicted XI, and only the surprise should move a posted price.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.measurement: Predict starters via a logistic model on last-5 starts, minutes, injury flags, rest, press-conference status (calibrated start probability p_i); expected lineup value E[V]=sum p_i * v_i; surprise = V_actual - E[V] in expected goals (v_i from ridge on team xG-diff). Compute at lineup release; as-of strictly the announced lineup timestamp.
soc.lineup_surprise_vs_predicted.why: Converts lineup information into a news variable with the right timing, which 'xi_strength_delta' alone cannot.

soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.label: Altitude difference between home venue and visitor's habitual altitude
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.mechanism: Home altitude minus the visitor's mean altitude over recent matches, with recency of exposure.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.rationale: Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia and Mexico City host matches above 2,000-3,600 m; visiting teams from sea level lose 0.3-0.6 goals of expected margin, the effect is nonlinear in altitude and decays with acclimatisation days, and is outside the usual home-advantage parameter.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.measurement: alt_gap = altitude(venue) - weighted mean altitude of visitor's matches in the last 60 days (weights half-life 20 days), set to 0 below 500 m gap; effect = max(0, alt_gap - 500)/1000 as piecewise; fit beta on historical results with team home advantage included; separate for first and second half if data permits.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.why: A first-order home advantage driver in the Bolivian, Ecuadorian and Colombian leagues in this ledger bucket.

soc.friendly_match_intensity.label: Friendly-match rotation and effort index
soc.friendly_match_intensity.mechanism: Competitive-intent indicator for friendlies and pre-season matches.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.rationale: Club friendlies settle like league games but are played with rotated squads, 60-minute starters and mass substitutions, so ratings fitted to competitive matches overstate team quality and understate randomness.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.measurement: Binary and ordinal: match type (friendly/ pre-season/ derby friendly), days to season start, tournament context; estimate effect on |goal difference| and draw rate relative to league matches with team fixed effects over 8 seasons; shrink to competitive baseline with k=30 matches; apply a variance multiplier and a compressed rating gap.
soc.friendly_match_intensity.why: Friendlies appear in the ledger bucket (KXCLUBFGAME) with settlement identical to competitive matches but a distinct data-generating process.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Core strength estimates feeding the 3-way probabilities.

soc.ratings.reason: Both fit attack/defence strengths from goals (Dixon-Coles) or xG; running both as separate inputs duplicates strength; keep one as the prior and the other as a robustness check.

soc.home_advantage.reason: Home advantage is team- and competition-specific and sizable (about 0.3-0.4 goals), with a need to zero it on neutral grounds.

soc.dixon_coles_low_score.reason: Shifts draw cells; league-level rho is small but matters for the draw leg.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: Team-pair draw tendencies persist weakly; the structural draw rate is mostly from goal environment.

soc.xi_strength_delta.reason: Lineup quality relative to season average; needs surprise vs predicted version.

soc.rotation_index.reason: Predicts lineup changes before release; useful with a forecasting horizon of 24 hours.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Stakes explain effort differences in dead rubbers, but magnitude is modest outside relegation and title fights.

soc.congestion_load.reason: Cumulative minutes explain rotation more than performance; small incremental power.

soc.gk.reason: Keeper effect is small and mostly absorbed in defensive ratings.

soc.referee.reason: Referee baselines have little predictive value for the result direction beyond penalty rates; high noise.

soc.market_odds.reason: Closing odds are a market-derived benchmark for calibration, not an independent input.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to ensure regulation-only labels for cups and friendlies.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Lineup vintage is the main late information; timestamp discipline crucial.

soc.motivation.reason: Motivation is defined from the same season-simulation leverage as stakes_leverage.

soc.rest_travel.reason: Rest and travel add small signals, separately modelled from congestion.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG is the unadjusted data for the adjusted ratings.

soc.formation.reason: Tactical system matchups are hard to measure pregame and have weak evidence.

soc.rivalry_intensity.reason: Derby flag has only small effects on goals/cards and is partly collinear with draw propensity.

interactions.mechanism: The result impact of a missing player scales with team dependence on him and with opponent strength; a surprise absence of a star in a close match moves P(win) by 5-8 points while the same absence in a mismatch barely matters.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress outcome on surprise times rating gap; compare to additive.

interactions.mechanism: Altitude adds to the home advantage only above roughly 1,500 m of gap and saturates for well-acclimatised sides, so the altitude effect is a threshold, not a linear piece of the home term.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit home effect by altitude bins in Bolivian/Ecuadorian leagues.

interactions.mechanism: Rotation is most likely precisely when stakes are low and the next match is bigger, so rotation times (1 - leverage) predicts strength cuts; stakes alone does not.
interactions.how_to_test: Interaction regression of lineup strength on rotation index and leverage.

interactions.mechanism: Draw probability is determined jointly by the expected goal difference (peaks at 0), the total goals (lower totals raise draws) and rho; a rating-only model gets the ordering right but misprices the draw because it ignores total-goal environment.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate P(draw) against total expected goals and gap; check by decile.

interactions.mechanism: In friendlies the effective rating gap is compressed (rotation, substitutions) and the variance is higher, so P(favourite win) is a flattened function of the rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate slope of win probability on rating gap separately for friendlies.

nonlinearities.shape: Ordered-logit style S-curve in rating gap for win probability; draw peaks at zero
nonlinearities.why: P(home win) and P(away win) are logistic in the gap, while P(draw) is hump-shaped; a linear gap feature cannot represent the draw leg.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise linear above 1500 m, saturating by 3000 m
nonlinearities.why: The physiological penalty to acclimatised visitors saturates at extreme altitude and is minimal below the threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: Asymmetric: bad surprises count more than good ones
nonlinearities.why: A key absence reduces output more than a returning starter raises it, since the market expects the star by default.

contract.settlement_definition: One binary per candidate: YES when the named player is announced as the winner of the named award for the stated season (sampled: 2026 Women's Ballon d'Or for the 2025-26 season). Co-winners split the payout: Yes on each recipient resolves to $1 divided by the number of tied recipients unless a separate Tie/Co-Winners market is listed, all other candidates resolve No, and if no award is given every participant market resolves No. Resolution depends on the official announcement by the awarding body, not on statistics. Only one live series is in the bucket (KXBALLONDORAWARD), a single sampled market.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple recipients are announced and no separate Tie/Co-Winners market is listed, Yes contracts on each recipient resolve to $1 divided by the number of tied recipients
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties pay fractional (1/n) so a joint-winner scenario has probability weight and a payoff below one; the expected value of a candidate includes the tie-split term.

rules_evidence.quote: If no award is given, all participant markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: If the award is cancelled or not awarded for the season, all candidates settle No, so the probabilities across candidates need not sum to one and a residual 'no award' mass exists.

variants_and_edge_cases: Only one ledger series (KXBALLONDORAWARD, status finalized) carries rules, so the rest of the awards family (KXBALLONDOR men's, KXSUPERBALLONDOR, KXPFAPOY, KXEPLPOY, KXWCAWARD) is listed under player_season_leader_and_awards and its settlement language is TITLE_ONLY.

The voting body, number of voters, scoring scale (journalist points scale of 15-12-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1 for the top ten) and the eligibility window are not in the market text; they are facts about the award, and they determine the joint distribution of vote shares and the tie probability (ties are very rare).

Awards revealed by leak before the ceremony (previous years' leaks reached media days early) change the information state; the contract settles on the official announcement, creating timing risk if different sources publish contradictory winners.

The same candidate appears in many markets (Super Ballon d'Or etc.), but each is a distinct award with a different voter pool and eligibility period; the 'for the 2025-26 season' wording ties the season window to the voting criteria.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official announcement of the awarding body (France Football / UEFA ceremony or equivalent for the named award), as published on its website and ceremony.

mechanism.summary: A voted award is decided by ballots, not by on-pitch counting, so the mechanism is a vote-share model. The candidate pool is narrowed to a few players by team trophies in the eligibility window (the Champions League and tournament results carry the highest weight, with weights varying by year); within a team-success tier, individual output and media narrative separate candidates. Ballots from a finite panel aggregate with noise and possible national bias, so close races are near coin flips and ties can occur and pay 1/n. Credible leaks before the ceremony are the dominant late information, and the contract settles on the official announcement with a no-award clause.

stages.name: Eligibility, season window and candidate pool
stages.description: The award covers a defined season window and the shortlist (30 nominees for the Ballon d'Or) removes most players; the realistic contenders are 3-6 players whose teams won the main trophies in the window. A player's candidacy is determined by season-level team success and visible individual output, not by statistics accumulated before the window opens.
stages.distribution: Small discrete candidate set; probability mass heavily concentrated (top 3 hold 80-90% of the price) with a long tail of outsiders.

stages.name: Team success coupling and tournament weighting
stages.description: Voters are strongly influenced by trophies: a Champions League winner with a decisive final performance or a World Cup/Euros winner takes the lead, and the weight of each trophy varies with the year (international tournament year versus none). The player's share of team success (goals, assists and decisive moments in knockout rounds) converts team outcomes into candidate vote share.
stages.distribution: Conditional-logit style: vote share is a softmax of a utility that is dominated by team trophies; heavy-tailed shifts when a final is won or lost.

stages.name: Individual production and narrative
stages.description: Within a team-success tier, goals and assists, big-match output and the media narrative separate candidates: a 'story' (injury comeback, record-breaking season) adds votes beyond counting stats. Production is measured over the season window, but only part of it is in voters' memory, with more weight on the final months.
stages.distribution: Smooth, right-skewed utility differences; narrative factors are unobserved and partially proxied by media share and previous awards (PFA/UEFA awards).

stages.name: Voter panel aggregation and bias
stages.description: Each voter ranks a top-N list and the points sum determines the winner; with a few dozen to a hundred voters, the margin between top candidates, voter nationality and regional bias (home-country voting), and the scoring scale determine the final ordering and the chance of a tie. Close races (within 5-10 points) are essentially noisy draws.
stages.distribution: Sum of discrete voter ballots; vote-total noise sd of about 3-6 points for 100 voters; ties rare but nonzero.

stages.name: Announcement information and leaks
stages.description: The winner is determined before the ceremony and can leak; pre-ceremony reporting (credible outlets, club statements, attendance of players) updates the probability sharply, and the contract settles on the official announcement. Injuries and availability matter only before the window closes, so most existing season-stat inputs are inert at that point.
stages.distribution: Jump process: probability moves to near 0/1 on credible news; otherwise slow drift.

talent_strength.note: Candidate quality and team trophy outcomes drive the vote utility.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent matchup in a voted award: candidates are compared by voters across the whole season and not head to head in a match, so matchup variables of the game archetypes have no role here beyond the finals that feed team success.

role_personnel.note: Role (forward/midfielder) shapes how production converts to votes; minutes matter for the season window.

availability_news.note: Injuries before the window closes matter; after that, leaked announcements matter.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching and tactical scheme enter only through team trophies and a forward's volume, which the team-success input already captures; no voter looks at tactics, so no separate coaching input is warranted for a voted award.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a ballot cast by journalists after the season; their effect is already inside the underlying season outcomes the voters see, so there is no environmental input for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Final and knockout events weigh more heavily in voters' memory.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics such as shots or touches are not the voters' criterion beyond the goals and assists they produce; keeping them would give a false sense of precision in a subjective vote.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goal conversion is only a partial signal because voters respond to totals regardless of luck.

distribution_variance.note: Vote-share distribution and aggregation noise determine the tail and ties.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Tournament year, stakes of trophies, and narrative.

officiating_rules.note: Match officials do not affect a vote; rules and eligibility windows of the award are contract matters and are handled under settlement, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Co-winner split, no-award clause, season eligibility window.

soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.label: Trophy weighting by year and competition for voters
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.mechanism: Estimated vote weight for Champions League, World Cup, continental championships and league titles in each award year.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.rationale: A Women's Ballon d'Or in a tournament year behaves differently from a non-tournament year; the weight a Champions League final carries versus a World Cup depends on the year, which a pooled model would blur.
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.measurement: From historical winners and top-5 results (2018-2025 Ballon d'Or male and female, plus Super Ballon d'Or), fit a conditional-logit with features: team won UCL, won World Cup/Euros/Copa/AFCON, won league, reached final, interaction with tournament-year dummy; regularised with ridge and cross-validated by leave-one-year-out; output feature weights with sd.
raw_data: historical vote tables with ranks and points
soc.trophy_event_weight_by_year.why: Isolates the dominant coefficient of the voting model and lets the model switch regimes by year.

soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.label: Voter panel aggregation and tie simulation
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.mechanism: Monte Carlo of ballots with a points scale, voter nationality bias and noise, giving winner and tie probabilities.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.rationale: Close races among two or three candidates are decided by ballots drawn from a distribution; the probability of a tie and the payoff split depends on the scale, voter count and variance.
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.measurement: Simulate N voters (about 100 for Ballon d'Or) each drawing a top-10 ranking from a Plackett-Luce model with candidate utilities u_i + voter noise; points 15,12,10,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1; add a home-nation bias term b for voters from the candidate's country (b about 0.3 in utility); run 10k draws; report P(win), P(tie). Parameters fitted to the historical distribution of winning margins.
raw_data: vote totals by candidate and voter lists
soc.panel_vote_aggregation_model.why: Provides winner and tie probabilities and the 1/n split payoff that the contract specifies.

soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.label: Pre-announcement leak and credible-report signal
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.mechanism: Reliability-weighted indicator that the winner has been leaked ahead of the ceremony.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.rationale: Previous awards have been leaked days ahead by outlets and club staff; a credible leak moves probability to near certainty and is the most informative late input, but a false leak is also possible.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.measurement: Event log of statements and reports about the winner with source tier (club/federation official, established journalist, aggregator), timestamp and content; estimate P(true | tier) from past award leaks with Beta prior (alpha=2,beta=1); update posterior odds by the likelihood ratio at each report; as-of strictly report time.
soc.pre_ceremony_leak_signal.why: The decisive late-moving information for voted awards; absent from the existing list.

soc.prior_award_momentum.label: Momentum from precursor awards and shortlists
soc.prior_award_momentum.mechanism: Results of precursor awards (UEFA Player of the Year, PFA, national awards) and shortlists as predictors.
soc.prior_award_momentum.rationale: Precursor awards share voters or taste with the target award and are announced earlier, so they are cheap pre-ceremony information.
soc.prior_award_momentum.measurement: Binary and rank features: won/placed in UEFA Women's Player of the Year, FIFA Best, PFA/WSL awards, league MVP; fit to historical winners with leave-one-out CV; weight by correlation of voter bodies.
soc.prior_award_momentum.why: Adds the predictability of taste before the target award.

soc.award_voting_narrative.reason: Voters respond to narrative and team success rather than counting stats; the conditional-logit on goals, trophies and media share is the right shape.

soc.player_awards.reason: Remaining-season Poisson production is defined for in-season scoring races; for a voted award decided after the season it is only a weak proxy for the narrative component.

soc.player_xg.reason: npxG/90 is not what voters weigh and the season window is closed by the time of the ceremony; keep only as a covariate for forward candidates.

soc.leader_race_state.reason: Scoring-race tally state belongs to Golden Boot-type contracts; for a voted award it adds nothing beyond goals in the season record.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Team trophy probabilities before the final matter; after the final they are deterministic.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Expected future minutes cannot affect a vote on a completed season; irrelevant once the season window has closed.

soc.injuries.reason: Injury status affects which candidates are in the race only before the end of the window; post-season it has no effect.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Regression to the mean concerns future production; voters judge realised totals, not expected ones.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed for co-winner split and no-award clauses.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook outright prices are market-derived and are only a calibration benchmark.

soc.shots.reason: Shot counts do not matter to voters beyond the goals they produce.

soc.award_vote_distribution.reason: Vote-share distribution fitted by conditional logit is the core model; should add year effect and aggregation noise.

interactions.mechanism: A player's vote share multiplies trophy weight by individual narrative: a Champions League winner with the key goal gets disproportionately more votes than the winner's teammate, so team success and individual role multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit with interaction between trophy won and decisive-contribution measure.

interactions.mechanism: Win probability is a threshold on the sign of the difference in vote totals, so the closer two candidates are, the more the noise term dominates and win probability goes towards 0.5; the odds are steep when margins exceed about 15 points.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated win probabilities with historical margin outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: Before a credible leak the market is in a model-driven regime; after it, probability jumps to near certainty regardless of the model, so the model prior is replaced by the reliability of the source.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of price/probability around leak timestamps.

interactions.mechanism: Precursor award results matter more when the Champions League final has been played and is undecided for the leader, because the leaders are already narrowed; before the final they are weaker evidence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast predictiveness of precursor awards by timing relative to major final.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax saturation: vote share concentrated in top two candidates
nonlinearities.why: Utility differences translate to win probability through a softmax, so a gap of one utility unit moves the leader from 50% to 73% while the tail candidates stay near zero.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at tournament-final result
nonlinearities.why: Winning the Champions League or the World Cup produces a discrete jump in utility rather than a gradual change.

contract.settlement_definition: Mixed bucket. Season-stat ladders (KXEPLSEASONSTAT 'records 14+ goals across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season', strike_type structured, floor 13.5) settle YES when the named player's season total reaches the integer N; leader markets (KX*LEADER, Golden Boot) settle YES for the player who finishes first in goals/assists, with tie treatment not visible in the sampled text; player-of-the-year awards (KXEPLPOY, KXPFAPOY, KXBALLONDOR) settle on a voted result. The bucket also contains about 25 First Team to Score series (KX*FTTS) which are match-level contracts: YES when the named team records the first goal of the entire game including stoppage and extra time, own goals credited to the team awarded the goal.

rules_evidence.quote: If Yoane Wissa records 14+ goals across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season-total threshold for a named player 'across all games' of that EPL season: the counting scope (EPL fixtures only, or cups too) is a wording question; a floor of 13.5 means the rung is 14 goals.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first goal of the match is an own goal, the market will resolve based on the team awarded the goal.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement of the First Team to Score series, mis-bucketed here, credits own goals to the beneficiary; this is a match-level first-event contract that does not belong with season totals.

rules_evidence.quote: The following market refers to a team in the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Unlike regulation-only match markets, FTTS counts the first goal across extra time, so a 0-0 after 90 that is decided by an ET goal still has a first scorer.

variants_and_edge_cases: Mixed contracts: season stat ladders, leader (top scorer or assister), voted awards and match-level first-team-to-score share one ledger key; the only mechanism common to all is that a final tally or a vote is read at a deadline, so one input list cannot serve all four.

Leader markets: tie rules (shared Golden Boot, tiebreak by assists/minutes) are not in the sampled text; a tie among leaders may pay 1/n like the voted award or resolve by official tiebreak, and the choice moves the price of the second candidate materially.

Season-stat counting scope 'across all games during the 2026-27 EPL season' may include only league games; a player transferring out mid-season (winter window) keeps only goals scored in the league before leaving or for the new club if both are in the league; this scope is not stated.

Only 2 of 46 series have rules text; KXEPLLEADER, KXLALIGALEADER, KXWCGBOOTGOALS and others are TITLE_ONLY, including World Cup variants in which only about 7 matches are played, so a different scale of the count process.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics (Premier League official site goal and assist records, awarding bodies for voted awards); the data provider's treatment of own goals, disallowed goals and assist attribution (Opta definitions) is not stated in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: For a season total or a leader market the outcome is the realised tally at the deadline: expected goals equals matches times minutes survival times team chance volume times the player's share times finishing, with penalty duty adding a discrete block. Minutes are a survival process with a zero-inflated left tail; finishing luck must be shrunk; teammates and managers change the share mid-season. A leader market is the maximum of many correlated tallies, so variance and tie rules matter as much as means. Voted awards and match-level first-team-to-score contracts are different mechanisms mis-bucketed here, and settlement depends on counting scope and tie language that are not visible for most series.

stages.name: Availability and minutes over the remaining season
stages.description: A player's tally can only grow while he plays; the remaining-season minutes distribution is determined by the injury hazard (with history of recurrence), suspensions, rotation and the risk of leaving the competition (winter transfer, loan), so expected minutes is a survival-type quantity. A starter with 85% of minutes in the first 12 games can lose a quarter of the remaining season to a single injury.
stages.distribution: Survival and recurrence process; minutes are zero-inflated with a mass at 0 (injury) and a bulk near 80-90 per start; heavy left tail.

stages.name: Per-match goal or assist intensity
stages.description: Per 90 the player scores according to shot volume, shot quality and finishing, plus penalty duty; role in the team (focal striker vs shared) determines the share of team xG, and teammate arrivals or departures change that share. Per-match intensity is combined with the opponent's defence and the team's expected goals for that fixture.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like per-match counts; strong dependence on set pieces and penalties; season totals are overdispersed relative to a Poisson with the mean xG.

stages.name: Luck versus skill in current tally
stages.description: The running total includes finishing over- or under-performance relative to xG which should be regressed toward the player's multi-season baseline; a striker at 12 goals from 7 xG is a regression candidate while another at 7 from 12 xG is not. The shrinkage fraction is large over a half season.
stages.distribution: Poisson noise plus persistent skill; finishing skill persists weakly (about 20-30% over a season).

stages.name: Race dynamics across candidates
stages.description: Leader markets are decided by the maximum across many correlated candidates: teammates compete for the same chances, candidates share fixtures, and ties and tiebreaks matter; the probability a candidate is first depends on the gap to the leader and on how many rivals are within reach, not on his own mean alone.
stages.distribution: Order-statistic outcome from a vector of correlated overdispersed counts; the maximum rewards variance (high-volume strikers with injury risk).

stages.name: Voted awards and narrative (sub-contract)
stages.description: Player-of-the-year contracts are decided by a panel or players' vote, so the mechanism there is team success and narrative rather than a counting stat; their relevant inputs overlap with those of the player_award archetype.
stages.distribution: Softmax vote-share with team trophy weighting; discrete winner.

stages.name: Settlement scope and mis-bucketed match events
stages.description: The contract reads the official total at season end (all games vs league only; own goals; disallowed goals) or the first-goal event of one match in the FTTS case; correct mapping of scope, tie rule and event type avoids label errors in training data.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from official statistics; scope ambiguity is the only randomness.

talent_strength.note: Per-90 scoring rates with opponent context; leaders are the top of a talent distribution.

opponent_matchup.note: Fixture difficulty and set-piece opportunity for each candidate.

role_personnel.note: Role, penalty duty, share of team shots, minutes.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and news flow; long horizon so status vintage matters less than hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager changes alter a striker's role and service, and a tactical shift (system change, new playmaker) can change goals per 90 by 20-30% in the middle of a season; no input quantifies this and press-conference news does not capture it.

environment.note: Weather and pitch effects on a single player's goal count are small and average out over dozens of matches; their impact is already in the per-90 rate, so no separate environmental input is required for a season total.

game_context_script.note: Current tally, matches remaining and the position relative to the leader.

pace_volume.note: Shot volume share of the player and of the team.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic race simulations and dispersion of totals.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Congestion and rotation across competitions affecting minutes.

officiating_rules.note: Referee identity affects penalties awarded to a given team only slightly over a season and averages out; it matters at the match level for first-event contracts, not for season-long leader totals, so no officiating input is attached here.

settlement_contract.note: Counting scope, tie rules, own-goal and disallowed-goal handling.

soc.team_goal_share_competition.label: Player's share of team npxG and competition for it
soc.team_goal_share_competition.mechanism: Share of team non-penalty xG taken by the player and how it changes with teammates.
soc.team_goal_share_competition.rationale: A player's goal rate equals team chance volume times his share; new signings, injuries to teammates and system changes redistribute shares in ways that per-90 averages miss, and a shared striker role halves volume in expectation.
soc.team_goal_share_competition.measurement: share_i = player npxG / team npxG over the last 20 matches (half-life 10) with shrinkage to position-role mean at k=8 matches; projected share = share adjusted by indicator of teammate arrivals/departures and rotation (regress change in share on competitor strength); expected goals = team npxG projection x share x P(playing).
raw_data: player-level shots and xG by match
soc.team_goal_share_competition.why: Separates team volume from role share, the quantity that changes when squads change.

soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.label: Remaining-season minutes survival curve
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.mechanism: Survival function of availability over the remaining matches including recurrence.
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.rationale: Minutes are the multiplier on every per-90 rate and are far from deterministic; injury recurrence, age and load create a left-skewed distribution; the cumulative effect over 25+ matches is what the season total needs.
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.measurement: Cox / discrete-time hazard model for injury onset per match with covariates age, previous injuries in 24 months, minutes last 28 days, position; plus duration model for time-out; simulate remaining season for each candidate; expected minutes and its quantiles; shrink the baseline hazard to the position mean with k=30 player-seasons.
raw_data: injury episodes with dates and durations
soc.season_minutes_survival_curve.why: Gives tails (long-term injury) that a mean minutes input misses.

soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.label: Leader tie rule and counting scope flags
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.mechanism: Contract-level flags for tie handling and which competitions count.
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.rationale: Leader prices are sensitive to whether a tie pays 1/n, goes to assists or minutes, or resolves No for all; and 'all games' versus 'league games' changes the tally by cup goals.
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.measurement: Parse and version rules_primary/secondary of each leader and season-stat series into flags: scope {league_only, all_competitions}, tie_rule {split, tiebreak_assists, tiebreak_minutes, official_source}, own_goal handling; resolution source; store with version hash and timestamp; for unsampled series mark UNKNOWN and require manual confirmation before use.
raw_data: rules text by series with timestamps
soc.leader_tiebreak_and_scope.why: Without it the same player goal tally is labelled differently across leader markets.

soc.leader_race_state.reason: Current tally, matches remaining and expected minutes are the state variables for the race simulation.

soc.player_xg.reason: Non-penalty xG/90 is the rate input; should be combined with team share and minutes survival.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes multiplies the rate; needs a survival distribution not a point estimate.

soc.penalty_taker_status.reason: Penalties are 10-20% of a top scorer's goals; designated taker status is a discrete share determinant.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Needed to avoid extrapolating hot finishing, though shrinkage is already built into the xG-based rate.

soc.injuries.reason: Current status matters, but the longer horizon is better served by the survival curve.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Opponent quality changes expected goals modestly for 20+ remaining matches.

soc.set_pieces.reason: Set-piece role is partly in xG; needed mainly for aerial forwards.

soc.award_voting_narrative.reason: Relevant only to the voted-award series sitting in this bucket, irrelevant to counting stats.

soc.player_awards.reason: Remaining-season Poisson race simulation is the same computation as the leader race-state input.

m.rules_text.reason: Tie rule and scope must be parsed per series; not a predictor.

soc.shots.reason: Raw shots add little over xG for finishing-driven goal counts.

soc.xg.reason: Team-level xG is the team context; the player-level rate subsumes the information once combined with team share.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Timestamped match lineups matter for single matches, not for a season-long total; marginal once the survival curve exists.

soc.press_conference_news.reason: News flows matter only for injuries and transfers; weak, noisy signal for a season-long contract.

interactions.mechanism: Expected goals equal team volume times share times minutes survival; the three factors multiply so an injury-prone high-share striker has high mean but a fat left tail, and the 14+ threshold is then crossed with a lower probability than the mean suggests.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare probability of crossing the strike from simulation with mean-only prediction.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of finishing first depends on tie rules: if ties split payouts, a candidate level with the leader has half the value, and if ties resolve on assists the playmaker striker gains; the gap-to-leader effect is conditional on the tie rule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate leader markets under each tie rule and compare to observed settlements.

interactions.mechanism: The expected future scoring rate is a shrunk mix of a hot finishing record and xG; the weight on realised goals decays with sample size, so equal over-performance is worth much less in a long remaining season.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest forward goals/90 on past npxG and past goals with an interaction in sample size.

interactions.mechanism: Penalty duty adds about 0.1 goals per match for the designated taker only if the team gets penalties; teams with an average of 0.15 penalties per match produce a threshold gain only for strikers, with the effect conditional on penalty-prone fixtures and VAR.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress goals on designated-taker flag and team penalty rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Left-skewed, zero-inflated minutes distribution
nonlinearities.why: Minutes are bimodal at injury (0) and full-minutes outcomes; linear expectations misprice exceedance probabilities for round-number rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Sigmoid in gap to leader scaled by sqrt(remaining expected goals)
nonlinearities.why: Probability of overtaking depends on gap relative to the sd of remaining goals; under 2 goals gap it is near-linear, beyond 5 it collapses.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with sample size
nonlinearities.why: Predictive weight on observed over-performance grows with shots taken, roughly n/(n+k) with k about 100 shots.

contract.settlement_definition: Table-position series (KX*LAST, KX*RELEGATION, KX*TOP/TOP4, KXEFLPROMO, KXBRASILEIROTOPX-style) settle YES when the named team finishes in the stated place or set of places in the final official table of the stated season; 'finishes in last place' is a single-rank event, relegation is a bottom-N event. Advancement series (KX*ADVANCE 'To Advance') settle YES when the named side advances past its opponent in the stated tie and round, e.g. 'Palmeiras advance past Fluminense in the Palmeiras vs Fluminense soccer tie in the Semi-Finals of the CONMEBOL Libertadores', so extra time and penalties count if the tie format uses them; the sampled texts do not say how a two-leg aggregate or tiebreak is applied.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tottenham finishes in last place in the league table in the 2026-27 EPL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Last-place market is a single bottom rank in the final table; it is not the same as relegation (bottom three), so the probability is an extreme-value event with its own tiebreak exposure.

rules_evidence.quote: If Palmeiras advance past Fluminense in the Palmeiras vs Fluminense soccer tie in the Semi-Finals of the CONMEBOL Libertadores, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Advancement resolves on who progresses from the named tie (both legs), not on a single match result, so first-leg state, away-goals rules and ET/penalties belong to the event.

rules_evidence.quote: If Latina advance past Grosseto in the Grosseto vs Latina soccer tie in the Round 2 of the Coppa Italia Lega Pro, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Same wording is used for single-leg cup ties, where advancement includes extra time and penalties, so the format (one leg vs two) is per competition and has to be looked up.

rules_evidence.quote: If Villarreal finishes in last place in the league table in the 2026-27 La Liga season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Confirms last-place wording is identical across leagues but tiebreak order (head-to-head in La Liga) differs by competition.

variants_and_edge_cases: Last-place and relegation have different cut lines: 'last place' needs the single lowest points total and its tiebreak (La Liga/Serie A head-to-head first, Premier League goal difference first), while relegation is bottom-N and also affected by relegation play-offs in some leagues (Bundesliga 16th-place play-off, Ligue 1).

Top-N and qualification series (KXEPLTOP, KXLIGUE1TOP4, KXUCLQUAL) depend on spillover rules: European places pass down when a domestic cup winner already qualifies, and the number of UCL spots varies by coefficient; the cut line is therefore itself random.

Advancement series pool single-leg cups, two-leg Libertadores/Sudamericana ties, play-offs and World Cup group qualification (best-third-place rule); the number of legs, ET/penalties and away-goals treatment are competition-specific and not in the sampled text.

168 live series, only 7 with rules text; the others (EFL promotion via play-offs, group qualification, World Cup advance) are TITLE_ONLY, and a sanction-driven table change after the last match is not addressed by sampled wording.
contract.settlement_data_source: Final official league table (governing body) for placement markets; official tie result including extra time and penalties for advancement markets; the competition's published regulations for tiebreaks and slot allocation.

mechanism.summary: Placement and advancement events are threshold events on random objects. For tables, each team's final points come from simulated remaining fixtures with uncertain strengths; last place is the minimum of closely spaced totals, relegation or top-N is a rank threshold whose cut line itself depends on cup winners, play-offs and sanctions. For ties, advancement is a sequential tree: first-leg state, second-leg goals shaped by aggregate lead, extra time with fatigue, and a near-coin-flip shootout. Group qualification adds tiebreak order and best-third rankings. Injuries, manager changes and administrative rulings are the shocks, and settlement depends on the competition's own regulations and tie rules.

stages.name: Team strength with uncertainty
stages.description: Both sides of a bubble race and both sides of a tie begin with opponent-adjusted strength and its posterior width; for bottom-of-table and last-place events the weakest teams are separated by small rating differences, so uncertainty width and short-memory form (new manager, injuries) dominate rankings among the bottom five.
stages.distribution: Posterior of latent strength with sd about 0.1 log goals; bottom-N membership is an order statistic of closely spaced values.

stages.name: Table state and the schedule left to play
stages.description: Remaining fixtures determine how points can still be earned: points gap to the cut line, number of matches remaining, strength and venue of the opposition (including direct clashes between rivals for survival or a slot), all of which determine a team's distribution of final points relative to the line.
stages.distribution: Sum of remaining match lotteries (0/1/3); variance of gap relative to cut line scales with matches remaining.

stages.name: Where the cut line sits
stages.description: For top-N, qualification and relegation the line is not fixed: the number of UCL/UEL places depends on coefficients and on whether the domestic cup winner already holds a place, relegation can be affected by play-offs or points deductions, and promotion through play-offs is a separate mini-tournament; the effective threshold is a random variable determined by other competitions.
stages.distribution: Discrete random threshold determined by cup winners and administrative rulings; effect is 0 or 1 place shifts with probabilities of 10-30% in the cup-spillover case.

stages.name: Tie formats: legs, extra time and penalties
stages.description: An advancement market is the product of a first-leg state, a second-leg match, and then if needed extra time and penalties; the first-leg score, the venue of the second leg, and the team's priorities in the next league match drive risk-taking, and shootouts are close to coin flips. Away goals no longer decide UEFA ties but may in some national cups.
stages.distribution: Sequential probability tree; aggregate lead changes the match goal rate and draw probability; shootout win near 50% with small skill edge.

stages.name: Group-stage qualification and cross-group ranking
stages.description: Group qualification (World Cup, Nations League, Champions League league phase) depends on points, goal difference, head-to-head and in expanded formats on ranking third-placed teams across groups; the order of tiebreaks and the final-day simultaneous matches create strong dependencies between teams.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution across teams and groups; tie-breaks create discrete jumps in qualification.

stages.name: Squad shocks and administrative events
stages.description: Injuries, international absences and suspensions shift strength during the run-in; sanctions (points deductions, licensing, administration) move teams across the line administratively, with probability mass concentrated at lower-profile leagues.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed strength shocks and rare discrete administrative events.

talent_strength.note: Strength distribution with posterior width, needed particularly for tightly spaced bottom teams.

opponent_matchup.note: Direct clashes between rivals and group opponents.

availability_news.note: Availability news; matters for ties more than for season-long placement.

coaching_scheme.note: Mid-season managerial changes ('new manager bounce') are a recognised driver of relegation-zone teams, yet no input quantifies their effect size or timing, and the catalog only holds a manager-change flag under transfers.

environment.note: Weather, altitude and pitch affect single matches and their influence on season placement averages out; for ties, neutral-site venues are encoded in the aggregate-state and home-advantage logic rather than as a separate environmental input.

game_context_script.note: Aggregate and table state set risk posture and win probabilities.

pace_volume.note: Volume stats such as possession or shots matter only via the goal-model strengths feeding the simulation; no independent volume variable determines a table position or tie advancement, so no pace input is attached.

distribution_variance.note: Order-statistic and tail structure of the table, especially at the bottom.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes, rotation priority and break effects.

officiating_rules.note: Administrative sanctions, abandonment and voided matches.

settlement_contract.note: Tiebreaks, slot allocation and the contract wording.

soc.european_slot_spillover.label: European slot spillover and variable cut line
soc.european_slot_spillover.mechanism: Probability distribution of the number of European places a league gets and how many reach the table.
soc.european_slot_spillover.rationale: A top-4 or qualification contract refers to a cut line that moves: the UEFA coefficient determines league allocation, and a domestic cup winner already qualified through the league moves the places down the table; so a 'top 4' price for fifth place is a function of cup results.
soc.european_slot_spillover.measurement: For each league-season: baseline number of UCL/UEL/UECL places by coefficient (UEFA published), plus P(cup winner already in higher slot) from the cup simulation, plus UCL/UEL title-holder entry path; effective cut line L = base - E where E in {0,1} with probability from simulation; recompute after each cup round; as-of date stamped.
soc.european_slot_spillover.why: Makes the qualification threshold a random variable rather than a constant, which the table simulation alone omits.

soc.last_place_extreme_value.label: Bottom-of-table extreme-value distribution
soc.last_place_extreme_value.mechanism: Probability each team ends with the lowest points total, and the gap structure at the bottom.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.rationale: Last place is the minimum of correlated points totals; the favourite for last place often has only 25-40% because others are within a few points, and the shape is not a simple function of a team's own rating.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.measurement: From the posterior-sampled season simulation: for each team compute P(rank=N), P(rank in bottom 3), gap to 3rd bottom and to 4th bottom at each as-of date; calibrate with historical bottom-team final points (shrunk league mean with k=5 seasons); correct tie rules in the minimum.
soc.last_place_extreme_value.why: Last-place contracts are minimum order statistics and are not equal to relegation odds.

soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.label: Advancement tree for single-leg and two-leg ties
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.mechanism: Round-by-round conditional probabilities given the legs, the first-leg score and the tie rules.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.rationale: Advancement is a state-dependent tree: after a first-leg win by 1-0, the second leg's draw/win probabilities differ from a pre-leg symmetrical model; format rules (ET, penalties, away goals) then determine the remaining branch.
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.measurement: State = (leg, aggregate before, venue). For second legs: simulate goals with team lambdas multiplied by state multipliers (trailing +20%, leader -10%) estimated from 15 seasons of European and cup second legs, shrunk with k=40 matches; P(advance) = P(agg win in 90) + P(agg level) * (P(ET win) + P(pens win)); P(pens win)=0.5 + small skill adjustments.
raw_data: tie results with leg scores, ET, penalties
soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.why: Provides the structured tree the existing inputs (aggregate state, ET model, shootout skill) only describe separately.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Season simulation produces the table distributions; needs dynamic cut line and tiebreaks.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Leverage is an output of the same season simulation; using it as an input is circular for a placement forecast.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Head-to-head vs goal difference order alters last-place and cut-line outcomes in tight races.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Rare but decisive for administrative events; coverage in lower leagues is thin.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Required for group qualification markets, but it is a derived simulation, not an independent measurement.

soc.second_leg_aggregate_state.reason: Aggregate state is the primary driver of second-leg risk posture and the draw probability.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: ET goal rate and shootout probabilities determine the tail of the advancement tree.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Posterior width matters for bottom-of-table clusters.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: Schedule asymmetry is a first-order driver for survival races in the run-in.

soc.injuries.reason: Key injuries shift strength but season-long evidence of effect size is weak.

soc.international_break_effect.reason: Evidence for a systematic effect on league points is small and mostly absorbed by lineup availability.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed to know single-leg vs two-leg and ET/penalty rules; not a predictor.

soc.motivation.reason: Defined from the same season Monte Carlo leverage as stakes_leverage.

soc.penalty_shootout_skill.reason: Persistent shootout skill is statistically weak in available samples and only matters in a small share of ties.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: Voided matches and abandoned competitions are rare but contract relevant.

soc.press_conference_news.reason: Noisy signal for injuries and rotation that matters only for ties; long-run placement markets barely respond.

interactions.mechanism: A fifth-placed team's 'top-4' probability is a step function of whether a domestic cup winner is already qualified; the cup result shifts the cut line by one place, giving a threshold jump in qualification odds that the league simulation alone does not include.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare qualification probabilities with and without the cup-spillover branch in past seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Second-leg goal and draw rates depend on the first-leg lead: a two-goal leader plays deep, lowering both teams' rates, while a one-goal trailing team pushes; the advancement probability conditional on first-leg margin is nonlinear.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin second legs by first-leg margin and compare draw rates and goals.

interactions.mechanism: Last-place probability is convex in rating uncertainty because the minimum of several tightly clustered totals is more sensitive to variance than the mean; widening the posterior increases odds for the second-worst team more than it reduces the worst team's.
interactions.how_to_test: Scale the posterior sd by 0.5-1.5 and track P(last) of the bottom 3.

interactions.mechanism: Direct clashes among survival rivals create paths where points tie; the tiebreak order then decides, so schedule effects interact with tiebreak only in narrow finishing scenarios.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute frequency of tie-resolved placements in simulations by league.

interactions.mechanism: A pending deduction or a final-day simultaneous kickoff changes the competitive regime: the deducted team goes from fighting for survival to a dead-rubber, shifting rotation and draw rates for its rivals.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study on matches following deduction announcements.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in games remaining
nonlinearities.why: Schedule asymmetry adds variance proportional to the number of games left and nearly vanishes in the final two rounds when only points and tiebreak matter.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed minimum order statistic
nonlinearities.why: The distribution of the lowest total has a skewed shape, and linear rating-gap predictors understate the probability of surprises.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by aggregate margin: 0, 1, 2+
nonlinearities.why: Aggregate leads change rates sharply at one goal and saturate beyond two as leaders sit deep.
