contract.settlement_definition: Off-field event contracts that resolve on an official or credibly confirmed fact inside a window: a named player transferring out of a club before a date (KXLAMINEYAMAL, KXCLUBCHANGEMBAPPE: permanent transfers, loans of any duration and contract termination/expiry all count), the player's next club (KXJOINCLUB/KXJOINRONALDO, a multi-outcome set where a loan or signing counts for the signing club and 'no change' resolves a separate outcome), a manager leaving by effective date (KXPOCHETTINOOUT: resolves on the effective date of departure, not announcement), a host country being announced (KXCOPAAMERICAHOST: every announced co-host resolves Yes), or a governing-body sanction stripping a count of titles (KXMANCITYTITLES: 'at least 8', as officially announced before 1 Jan 2028).

rules_evidence.quote: This includes permanent transfers out (the player is sold or transferred to another club, whether for a fee or as a free transfer), loans out
rules_evidence.establishes: Loans of any duration count as leaving, so a loan-and-return still resolves YES; the event is broader than a permanent sale and the hazard of a loan must be included.

rules_evidence.quote: If Erling Haaland signs with a club and is immediately loaned out, the signing club resolves to Yes and all others resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: In the next-club set a 'sign-and-loan' credits the signing club, not the loan club, which affects multi-outcome probabilities for intermediaries.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple host countries are announced to host the 2028 Copa America
rules_evidence.establishes: Multiple co-hosts resolve Yes for each named; the host-country events are therefore not mutually exclusive and probabilities across countries can sum above one.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves solely based on the effective date of Mauricio Pochettino's departure from Manager of the US Men's National Team.
rules_evidence.establishes: Announcement or resignation timing is irrelevant; only the effective date counts, which can lag the announcement (notice periods) and matters near the deadline.

rules_evidence.quote: as officially announced before January 1, 2028
rules_evidence.establishes: Stripping of titles needs an official announcement by the deadline, so the timeline of a legal process (hearings, appeals) is the binding factor, not the merits alone.

variants_and_edge_cases: Sign-and-loan, contract-expiry release and transfers within the same group are all explicitly handled in the transfer series: a free-agent signing counts like a fee, and a player still at his club on the end date resolves a separate 'no change' outcome, so mutually exclusive outcomes must include 'no move'.

Governance events (host announcement, sanctions, bans) depend on committee calendars and appeal processes with fat-tailed timing; the stated window can end before a decision, which resolves No by default.

Manager markets (Pochettino out, next manager of clubs, Managers Out) resolve on effective date of departure or appointment; interim appointments and caretakers may not count, which the sampled text does not say.

Only 7 of 41 series have rules text; the next-manager, retirement and FIFA/UEFA governance series (KXNEXTMANAGERJUV, KXFIFALEAVE, KXUEFAISRAELBAN) are TITLE_ONLY, and the 'Source Agencies' definition for host announcements is not shown.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official club, federation or governing-body announcement (club websites, FIFA/UEFA/CONMEBOL communications), with credible news agencies as source agencies where named; effective dates as stated in the announcement.

mechanism.summary: An off-field soccer contract is a rare-event hazard resolved by an official announcement inside a window. The prior comes from a reference class (club state, player or manager profile, body and process type); the actor's fundamentals (contract end and release clause, results versus expectation, legal stage) tilt the hazard; the calendar (window deadlines, committee dates, effective dates) decides whether the event can occur before the contract's end; and information arrives as tiered reports whose reliability sets how far probability should jump. Multi-outcome sets (next club, co-hosts) need 'no change' and non-exclusive handling, and loans, sign-and-loan and effective-date wording must be read per series.

stages.name: Reference-class base rate in the window
stages.description: Each event type has a base rate that depends on its reference class: a top-club star leaving in a given calendar year, a manager at a given league position being dismissed within a season, a host selection by a given body; the window length, the starting state of the actor (tenure, contract, league position) and the structural calendar anchor the prior before any news.
stages.distribution: Rare-event hazard with prior from event counts per class; a few percent per month for a star player's departure, much higher for a bottom-table manager.

stages.name: Actor fundamentals and incentives
stages.description: A transfer requires a willing player, a willing seller and a buyer that can afford the fee and wages: contract expiry date, release clause, club finances, squad needs and the player's stated intentions determine feasibility; managers face board tolerance linked to results, owners and succession options; sanctions depend on evidence and legal process.
stages.distribution: Discrete-time hazard conditional on contract and club state; strongly nonlinear in months to contract end.

stages.name: Calendar and timing structure
stages.description: Transfers cluster at window deadlines (the last 72 hours account for a large share of summer-window deals), managerial dismissals follow poor-result runs and international breaks, and governance decisions follow committee dates and appeal periods. A contract whose window ends before a calendar decision date will resolve No whatever the merits.
stages.distribution: Event times clustered at deadlines; heavy-tailed delay distributions for regulatory processes.

stages.name: Information flow and credibility
stages.description: News arrives in tiers: club/federation statements, established journalists' 'here we go' confirmations, rumours from aggregators; the likelihood ratio of each tier and the lag from leak to official confirmation determine how fast a probability should move, and a false report is common at lower tiers.
stages.distribution: Jump process in log odds with reliability-dependent jump sizes; confirmation lag of hours to weeks.

stages.name: Governance and legal process
stages.description: Host selections and sanction decisions are decided by named bodies with procedural stages (bid evaluation, hearings, ruling, appeal) and politics; the events are lumpy, with long periods of nothing and sudden announcements; the stripping of a specific count of titles is a multi-valued legal outcome.
stages.distribution: Staged process with random stage durations and lumpy outcomes; multi-valued legal outcome (0, 1, 2, ... titles).

stages.name: Settlement mapping and multi-outcome bookkeeping
stages.description: Settlement uses effective dates and official announcements; the 'next club' and host sets must include 'no change' and multiple co-host cases; loans count in some contracts and not in others, so label construction requires reading each series' wording.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from announcement records; ambiguity is in definitions.

soc.contract_expiry_release_state.label: Contract expiry, release clause and renewal-talk state
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.mechanism: Months to contract end, release clause and wage structure, and reported renewal status.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.rationale: A transfer or release hazard is steeply nonlinear in months to contract end: under 12 months the selling club sells or the player leaves free; above 36 months only a release clause or a rebellion moves the player.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.measurement: For each player: months_to_expiry at as-of; indicator and amount of a release clause (if public) relative to market value; wage as % of club wage bill; renewal status {talks, agreed, stalled}; build hazard model h(months, status) fitted to 15 years of top-league transfers (discrete-time logit) with club-type effects; shrink to league rates with k=20 cases.
soc.contract_expiry_release_state.why: Directly drives KXLAMINEYAMAL-style leave-club contracts and next-club sets.

soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.label: Window calendar and deadline-clustering hazard
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.mechanism: Timing of open and closed windows and the daily hazard within them.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.rationale: Contracts ending before the window opens (e.g. 'before Jan 1, 2027' with a winter window opening only on 1 January) give a different probability than the same question in summer; deals cluster in the last days of a window.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.measurement: Build calendar of windows by league and country (summer, winter, extended Saudi/Turkish windows); estimate daily hazard share = fraction of deals by days-to-deadline from 10 years of data; probability a deal occurs before date D = integral of window-open days times hazard; adjust for emergency loans and free-agent signings outside windows.
soc.transfer_window_calendar_hazard.why: Prevents time-window errors that dominate short-dated transfer contracts.

soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.label: Manager dismissal and appointment hazard
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.mechanism: Hazard of leaving a role given results, expectations and board context.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.rationale: Managers are dismissed after results fall below expectation, with a spike after 4-6 game winless runs, and the 'next manager' contracts depend on the shortlist; national-team coaches depend on tournament cycle.
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.measurement: Cox model: hazard of leaving per matchweek on points-per-game minus expected points-per-game from ratings, league position relative to preseason rank, run of winless games, tenure, owner change; fit to 20 seasons of top-5 league managerial changes; shrink team-specific frailty with k=3 seasons; for national teams use cycle stage and tournament result.
raw_data: manager appointments and exits with dates and results
soc.manager_dismissal_hazard.why: Needed for KXPOCHETTINOOUT and Next Manager series with no existing input.

soc.governance_procedure_stage.label: Stage and expected timeline of governance procedures
soc.governance_procedure_stage.mechanism: Procedural stage of a sanction or bid process with historical stage durations.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.rationale: A sanction or host decision resolves only after a sequence of steps; the stated deadline can lapse during a hearing, so timeline and stage durations determine the probability more than the merits.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.measurement: Record procedure stage (allegation, hearing scheduled, hearing concluded, ruling, appeal) with dates; fit stage-duration distributions (log-normal) from comparable cases (financial fair play, UEFA sanctions, FIFA bids) and compute P(final decision before deadline) and the distribution of outcomes (e.g. number of titles stripped) by case type; as-of date stamped.
soc.governance_procedure_stage.why: Provides the timing probability that dominates Man City-type and host-selection contracts.

interactions.how_to_test: Fit the hazard model with an interaction between months to expiry and a window-open indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Without credible news the prior drifts slowly; after a top-tier confirmation the probability jumps near certainty irrespective of the base rate, so the information regime replaces the base-rate regime.

interactions.mechanism: A dismissal changes the transfer outlook for the club's stars (new manager's priorities) and vice versa; manager exits often precede window activity, so one hazard is conditional on the other state.
interactions.how_to_test: Cross-lagged analysis of manager change and star departures within 60 days.

interactions.mechanism: The probability of a final decision before the deadline is piecewise in stage: near zero before hearing, rises after ruling, and appeal windows add a second step; the number of titles stripped depends on appeal outcomes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conditional probabilities per stage from past cases.

interactions.mechanism: A star with a short contract at a club that has just lost its manager and sold others has a hazard far above the product of separate effects, because the club's bargaining position and the player's incentive both shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress departure on interactions of contract months and club transition indicators.

nonlinearities.shape: Steeply convex in months to expiry below 12
nonlinearities.why: Hazard of leaving rises sharply as expiry approaches because the club must sell or lose the player for free, so the function is not linear in months.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in time-to-event
nonlinearities.why: Governance and transfer timings have fat tails; the survival function is not exponential and a constant hazard overstates short-window probabilities.

nonlinearities.shape: Spike in daily hazard at the deadline
nonlinearities.why: Daily hazard is highly non-uniform: a disproportionate share of window deals complete in the final days, so cumulative probability by date is convex until the deadline.

contract.settlement_definition: The only live series (KXWINSTREAKMANU) is not a season points-total or margin contract: YES when Manchester United (men's) win at least 5 games in a row across all competitions in calendar year 2026, floor_strike 4.5 'greater'. The catalog target (team season points relative to a strike, or a points gap between two teams) has no live series in the ledger, so those variants are unverified. For the streak contract what counts as a win (90 minutes vs extra time/penalties), whether friendlies and Super Cups count as 'competitions', and whether a streak must lie entirely within 2026 are not stated in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: If Manchester United win at least 5 games in a row across all competitions in the year 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The event is a run-length statistic over the chronological sequence of all matches in the year; a draw or loss resets it and the number of matches in the remaining year is itself uncertain because cups can eliminate the team.

rules_evidence.quote: Will Manchester United men's soccer win at least 5 games in a row this year?
rules_evidence.establishes: Title restricts to the men's team and a calendar-year window; early-2026 wins before the as-of date already count toward a streak in progress.

variants_and_edge_cases: Win-streak runs depend on the order of fixtures: five consecutive opponents of average strength give p^5 around 0.05-0.08 for a team with p=0.55-0.6, but a favourable stretch of weak opponents multiplies the probability several times over, so the fixture sequence is the object, not the average quality.

In cup matches that go to extra time and penalties, whether a shootout win counts as a 'win' is not visible in the sampled rules; this changes the streak probability in cup fixtures (about 6-10% of cup ties go to shootouts).

A streak that began in late 2025 and is still running on 1 January 2026 counts only from the first 2026 win unless the wording says otherwise; only matches played inside calendar 2026 are counted and no 'across calendar year boundary' rule is shown.

No live series exists for season points totals or point margins between two teams in the ledger; the 'unreg' season-total family might exist elsewhere, so the catalog's target for this archetype is unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match results from the league or competition records (Premier League, FA Cup, UEFA competitions) for the named club; treatment of shootouts and friendlies is not stated.

mechanism.summary: The live contract is a run-length event: at least five consecutive wins in the chronological list of a team's matches in a calendar year. Each match has a win probability (draws and cup shootouts matter), the ordered sequence of remaining fixtures and their number (cup elimination can cut it short) determine how many five-match windows exist, shared strength uncertainty and a weak form persistence correlate consecutive matches, and rotation or injuries create regimes inside a congested stretch. The probability is computed by dynamic programming over the sequence rather than from average strength. Season-total and margin variants named by the archetype have no live series, so their settlement is unverified.

stages.name: Per-match win probability
stages.description: Each remaining match gets a win probability from the team's opponent-adjusted strength, the opponent's strength, venue and competition type; because only wins count (not draws), the relevant quantity is P(win), which is lower than 1-P(loss) by the draw probability, and the draw propensity of the pairing reduces the streak chance.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per match with p between 0.25 (away at a top side) and 0.85 (home against a weak side); sequence-dependent through shared strength uncertainty.

stages.name: Fixture sequence, count and survival in cups
stages.description: The year's remaining matches are an ordered list across league, domestic cups and Europe; each cup tie can end the team's participation (removing future matches) and the number and ordering of matches in the next weeks determines how many five-match windows exist. Ties decided on penalties must be classified (win or not) per the wording.
stages.distribution: Random-length ordered sequence; number of remaining matches around 25-35 with cup survival random; window-count is the number of overlapping 5-match segments.

stages.name: Run-length probability with dependence
stages.description: The probability of a 5-run is computed over the sequence of p_t with dependence induced by shared strength uncertainty and form regimes; positive serial correlation in match outcomes (beyond what ratings explain) raises streak probability relative to independence, and a hot-hand effect is weak but present through managers' tactical regimes and squad cohesion.
stages.distribution: Run-length distribution of a non-homogeneous Bernoulli sequence with positive latent correlation; streak probability can be 1.3-2 times the independent calculation over a season.

stages.name: Rotation, injuries and fatigue across the stretch
stages.description: Congested weeks cause rotation (lower p in cup or league matches that follow a European night), and an injury to a key player during the stretch lowers p across the remaining games in the window; the streak is most vulnerable in the middle of a busy December/spring schedule.
stages.distribution: Regime shifts in p_t by rotation and injury states; effect size 0.03-0.10 per-match p.

stages.name: Settlement and contract scope
stages.description: The count of wins and the chronology depend on the contract scope (all competitions, men's, calendar year), which games qualify as 'win' and the effect of postponements and abandonments on the order of matches; for season-total variants, the points total is the sum of 3W+D and the margin is the difference of two totals with deductions.
stages.distribution: Deterministic from official records; ambiguity in scope definitions.

talent_strength.note: Team strength and posterior width determine every p_t and their correlation.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent identity of each match in the sequence.

availability_news.note: Availability news for the matches in the next weeks; vintage matters less over a multi-month window.

coaching_scheme.note: A managerial change or tactical regime shift mid-year changes every p_t in the sequence at once; the existing inputs do not quantify managerial effects and a change would dominate a streak probability.

environment.note: Venue and weather enter through each match's win probability (home advantage is in the match model); the streak contract adds no environmental mechanism of its own beyond home/away order, which sits in the sequence vector.

game_context_script.note: Order of fixtures and the number of overlapping windows.

pace_volume.note: Volume statistics matter only through team ratings; a run-length contract is about win/not-win and no count of possessions or shots enters its settlement.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck versus skill in the current streak or form is regressed through xG-based ratings.

distribution_variance.note: Positive serial correlation and the run-length distribution.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rotation in congested weeks and cup priorities.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating tendencies affect single matches (penalties, cards) with no systematic influence on a multi-match streak over a year beyond the match-level win probabilities already estimated.

settlement_contract.note: Scope of competitions, win definition and postponements.

soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.label: Ordered vector of per-match win probabilities with cup survival
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.mechanism: Match-by-match P(win) for all scheduled and possible future fixtures in the contract window.
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.rationale: A streak is a property of the ordered sequence, not of the average opponent strength; two seasons with the same average p can differ by factor 2-3 in P(5-run), and cup rounds introduce randomness in which matches exist.
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.measurement: For each scheduled league/cup/European fixture: p_t = P(win in 90 min [+ ET/pens per rule]) from the goal model with venue, rest and lineup scenario; for future cup rounds weight by survival probability s_t; compute vector with dates; P(run>=5) by dynamic programming on the run-length Markov chain, including the current streak count c0; as-of = prior to the next match.
soc.fixture_sequence_win_vector.why: The exact object of the streak contract; none of the existing inputs defines the ordered sequence.

soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.label: Scope flags: competitions counted and what counts as a win
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.mechanism: Parsed contract flags for which fixtures count and how extra-time or penalty wins are treated.
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.rationale: The same team and schedule gives different probabilities if friendlies and the Community Shield count, or if shootout wins count as wins; scope can change the probability by 20% or more.
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.measurement: Parse rules text for flags: competitions_all vs league_only, friendlies_count (bool), shootout_win_counts (bool), men_only, calendar window; store as version-hashed record per series; unknown flags remain UNKNOWN and require manual check; the sequence builder filters fixtures accordingly.
soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.why: Removes label ambiguity before any probability is computed.

soc.latent_form_persistence.label: Latent form persistence (serial correlation of match residuals)
soc.latent_form_persistence.mechanism: Autocorrelation of match outcome residuals beyond ratings and strength drift.
soc.latent_form_persistence.rationale: If outcomes carry positive serial correlation after controlling for strength, runs are more likely than the independent calculation; if it is zero, ratings with drift suffice. Estimating it matters because the streak is a run statistic.
soc.latent_form_persistence.measurement: Fit a state-space model: match residual e_t = result - expected from ratings; AR(1) coefficient phi estimated across all clubs in top-5 leagues over 10 seasons with club random effects and drift variance; report phi with interval; use phi to generate correlated Bernoulli via a latent Gaussian copula; as-of prior matches only.
raw_data: match results for top leagues over 10 seasons
soc.latent_form_persistence.why: Calibrates streak odds to empirical clustering; the hot-hand effect is small, but multiplies the run probability.

soc.points_total_distribution.reason: Season-total distribution machinery is right for the catalog's points contracts but is only a by-product for the streak, which needs the ordered sequence.

soc.remaining_schedule_strength.reason: The order and venue of remaining opponents is the deterministic component; average strength alone hides the sequence.

soc.ratings_uncertainty.reason: Shared strength uncertainty is what creates positive correlation between consecutive matches.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Per-match win probabilities require opponent-adjusted strengths.

soc.draw_propensity.reason: A win-only contract is hurt by draws, so pairing draw tendency lowers P(win) beyond the rating gap.

soc.points_deductions.reason: Points deductions do not affect match wins in a streak; irrelevant to the only live series.

soc.injuries.reason: Key injuries lower p across a window; need vintage near the streak window.

soc.paired_team_correlation.reason: Two-team correlation is for margin series between teams, not for a single-team run.

m.rules_text.reason: Scope of competitions and win definition; not a predictor.

soc.xg.reason: Raw xG is the unadjusted base of the adjusted ratings.

soc.motivation.reason: Stakes leverage (title/relegation) is rarely informative for a team's match-to-match win probability beyond rotation, which is covered by lineups.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: Postponements move fixtures in and out of the window and alter order.

interactions.mechanism: Streak probability is the product of ordered p_t modified by latent correlation: with phi>0 a favourable stretch is more likely to continue, so correlation raises P(5-run) most when the sequence has several strong p_t in a row.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare dynamic-programming independent probabilities to the copula version on historical streak outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: Uncertainty in strength widens the distribution of p across the window; because run probability is convex in p (p^5), higher variance of p raises the expected run probability, so a wider posterior increases streak odds for the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare streak odds under fixed vs sampled strength using the same sequence.

interactions.mechanism: If shootout wins count, cup ties become near-50% 'wins' in drawn matches, raising p for cup fixtures; if not, a drawn cup match breaks the streak. The scope flag therefore conditions the sequence vector.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(streak) under each scope setting and report the spread.

interactions.mechanism: A key injury during a rotation-heavy fortnight lowers p more than either alone; below a squad-depth threshold the rotation weakens multiple fixtures at once and streaks break.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate p_t change in matches with injury and rotation together vs alone.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex (power of five) in per-match win probability
nonlinearities.why: The streak probability is roughly the sum over windows of the product of five p_t; a 0.05 change in p changes P(streak) by about 40% relative to its size.

nonlinearities.shape: Weak positive phi with threshold effect near 0.05
nonlinearities.why: Persistence only changes streak probability materially once phi exceeds roughly 0.05; below it the independent computation suffices.

contract.settlement_definition: YES when the combined goals of both teams exceed the x.5 strike in the 90 minutes plus stoppage time of the match ('If over 5.5 goals are scored ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)'); team-total series (KXUECLTEAMTOTAL, KXCONMEBOLSUDTEAMTOTAL) use the same window for a single team's goals. Own goals count for the team awarded the goal; strikes are half-goals so no push exists; the ladder of strikes (observed 5.5, 6.5, 7.5 and presumably lower rungs) is a nested monotone set of events. Cancelled or rescheduled-beyond-48-hours matches settle at fair price per the generic game text.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 5.5 goals are scored in the Algeria vs Togo professional AFCON Qualifiers soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Totals strikes are high (5.5) in this sampled series: P(6+ goals) is a deep-tail event of about 2-4% in qualifiers with mismatched sides, so tail calibration matters more than the mean.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 5.5 goals are scored in the Besiktas vs Genclerbirligi professional Super Lig soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: Same wording across leagues; the 5.5 line on a league match with a strong home side is a mismatch tail contract.

rules_evidence.quote: after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties)
rules_evidence.establishes: Extra time goals are excluded; in cup totals a 2-2 after 90 that finishes 4-3 in ET is still 4 goals, and ET must not be included in training labels.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 7.5 goals are scored in the Kabilio Jaffa vs Ironi Modiin professional State Cup soccer game
rules_evidence.establishes: The ladder extends to 7.5 in a cup tie between mismatched Israeli clubs, i.e. the tail of the count distribution beyond seven goals is a live contract.

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike ladder: each rung is P(total >= k+1), monotone decreasing; rungs at 5.5-7.5 are extreme tail events that exist because of mismatches (cups, women's matches) and are mis-modelled by Poisson with league-average mean.
Team-total series (KXUECLTEAMTOTAL, KXEPLTEAMTOTAL-style) require a single side's count; an own goal credited to the side counts, so the opponent's attack feeds a team's count at about 3-5% of goals.

Totals for halves (1H/2H) are in first_half_and_period, and the same 'Point Total' ledger title is used for goals totals; league and cup versions differ in incentives (aggregate scores, ET) while settlement is regulation-only.
202 live series, 4 sampled with rules; other leagues are TITLE_ONLY and are presumed identical; abandonment mid-match with goals already scored is not addressed.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match report final regulation score (home goals plus away goals, own goals credited to the beneficiary) from the competition's governing body; extra time and penalties excluded.

mechanism.summary: Total goals is the sum of two correlated overdispersed counts settled at 90 minutes plus stoppage. The mean comes from opponent-adjusted attack and defence strengths and the league's goal environment; the lineup's attack and defence composition moves the two sides in opposite directions, so it needs a split rather than a scalar. A shared latent openness factor correlates the team counts and thickens both tails; game-state damping and mismatch collapses shape the right tail, which is what the high rungs (5.5 to 7.5 in the sampled series) price. Finishing and keeper luck, set-piece and penalty events, weather and referee tendencies add noise, and the ladder is a nested monotone set with regulation-only settlement.

stages.name: Two scoring intensities and their sum
stages.description: The total's mean is the sum of both teams' opponent-adjusted lambdas; the lineup's attack/defence composition (which attackers and which defenders play) determines each side's contribution separately, and the sum rewards openness on both sides. League goal environment, home goal share and season trend set the baseline, with strong cross-league differences (2.3 to 3.3 goals per match).
stages.distribution: Sum of two overdispersed counts; mean around 2.7 with variance about 10-15% above Poisson once state effects included.

stages.name: Shared openness and style factor
stages.description: Some matches are open for both sides (high lines, weak defences, derbies without stakes) and some closed (cautious, low blocks); this match-level latent factor correlates the two teams' scoring and thickens both tails of the total beyond independent Poisson, which is why 0-0 and 5-3 are both more common than the independent model predicts.
stages.distribution: Mixture over a latent openness variable; positive correlation between team counts at the match level, negative conditional correlation within game-state.

stages.name: Game-state and tail dynamics
stages.description: Once a lead builds the leader eases off, so tails are shaped by two competing forces: collapse of a weaker team (red card, mismatch) pushes the total upward in bursts, while garbage-time damping caps it; the net is a heavy right tail only in strongly mismatched fixtures and in leagues with poor defending. High strikes depend on the tail, not the mean.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail from mismatch mixture; P(total>=7) well above Poisson tail in cups with divisional gaps.

stages.name: Finishing, keeper and set-piece luck
stages.description: Realised totals include finishing and goalkeeper variance: a keeper in hot form or a team that has overperformed xG for months is a regression candidate, and set-piece and penalty events add lumpy goals; weather (wind, rain) modifies shot quality and keeper handling modestly.
stages.distribution: Overdispersion from persistent skill plus transient luck; penalty events add about 0.25-0.3 goals per match in expectation with high variance.

stages.name: Ladder and settlement
stages.description: Rungs form a monotone ladder in P(total>k); the contract uses regulation goals including stoppage, and team totals use one side's count; extra time and shootouts are excluded; cross-rung consistency is a constraint, not an input.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping; ladder is an implied distribution.

soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.label: Calibrated tail dispersion of match totals by league and mismatch bucket
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.mechanism: Excess probability of 5+ and 6+ goal matches relative to independent Poisson, by league and expected-total bucket.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.rationale: High strikes (5.5-7.5) are tail contracts: Poisson with league-average mean misses by factors of two, and the tail multiplier depends on mismatch size and league defending quality.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.measurement: Pool 10 seasons per league; bin matches by model expected total (deciles) and expected absolute goal difference; compute observed P(total>=k)/model P for k=4,5,6,7; isotonic smoothing; hierarchical shrinkage across leagues with k=150 matches per bin; output tail multiplier function m(league,bucket,k); as-of prior matches only.
soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.why: The sampled strikes of 5.5 to 7.5 make tail multipliers the first-order calibration term.

soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.label: Match-level shared openness factor
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.mechanism: Latent factor that moves both teams' scoring rates together, estimated from residual correlation.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.rationale: Totals are controlled by how open the match is for both sides, which is more than the sum of two independent rates; ignoring it understates both 0-0 and 5-goal frequencies.
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.measurement: Fit a bivariate model with a shared log-normal factor: log lambda_home = a_h - d_a + gamma*z, log lambda_away = a_a - d_h + gamma*z, z~N(0,1); estimate gamma per league by marginal likelihood over 5 seasons; also the team-pair covariates: both teams' PPDA and line height difference; shrink gamma toward the league value with k=30 matches per team-pair class.
raw_data: match scores and team style metrics
soc.shared_openness_latent_factor.why: Directly models correlation between the team counts that drives the tails of totals.

soc.xi_attack_defence_split.label: Lineup attack and defence value split
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.mechanism: Separate expected-goals deltas for the attacking and defending halves of the confirmed XI.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.rationale: A scalar lineup-strength delta cannot say whether goals will rise or fall: a missing centre-back raises the total while a missing striker lowers it, and these may cancel in a scalar.
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.measurement: From a ridge regression on team xG for and against per match on minutes-weighted player indicators (separate models for xG_for and xG_against), compute attack_delta = sum over starters of player_attack_value minus season-average XI value, and defence_delta likewise (including the keeper); expected total change = attack_delta_h + attack_delta_a + defence_delta_h + defence_delta_a (signs per convention); evaluate at lineup release.
raw_data: player xG and xGA on/off, lineups
soc.xi_attack_defence_split.why: Totals respond to the sum of attack and defence changes with different signs for each side.

interactions.mechanism: Both teams' lambdas are multiplied by the same latent openness factor, so the total rises as the product and its variance increases with the sum of lambdas; mismatches amplify the tail more than balanced games.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit gamma by league and check calibration of P(total>=5) in high-lambda games.

interactions.mechanism: A missing centre-back raises the total only if the opponent has strong attackers, and a missing striker lowers it only if the team's chances are concentrated in him; effects are conditional on matchup and on the lineup actually announced.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress totals on defence_delta times opponent attack quality.

interactions.mechanism: Tails switch regime with lead size: up to a three-goal gap totals grow, beyond it damping or collapse dominates, so tail multipliers must condition on the expected gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tail multipliers within bins of expected absolute goal difference.

interactions.mechanism: Heavy rain or wind lowers the effectiveness of high-tempo passing teams more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals is scaled by the style of the teams playing.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact weather indicators with team passing-directness index.

interactions.mechanism: Totals depend on both teams' finishing and both keepers; hot finishing against a hot keeper nets out; the joint distribution of finishing and keeper residuals sets the variance, not each separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare totals variance with joint shrinkage of finishing and keeper residuals vs separate.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in league mean but convex in rung probability at 5.5+
nonlinearities.why: A 0.2 shift in league average goals changes P(total>=6) by more than 20% relative because the tail is exponential in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Monotone isotonic multiplier increasing with k
nonlinearities.why: Tail multiplier relative to Poisson is not constant across rungs: it is about 1.0 at 2.5 but 1.5-2.5 at 6.5 and above.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in wind speed above about 30 km/h
nonlinearities.why: Weather affects scoring materially only beyond thresholds (strong wind, heavy rain), with near-zero effect otherwise.

contract.settlement_definition: All six live series are corner counts: combined ('Ipswich Town and Bournemouth combined record at least 9+ corners') or single-team ('Ipswich Town records at least 5+ corners') thresholds of the form N+ (floor_strike N, greater_or_equal) over the entire game, which per the sampled text includes regulation, stoppage and any extra time. In the EPL/La Liga versions only corner kicks actually taken count; awarded-but-not-taken corners do not. There is no live series for cards or fouls, so the catalog label 'corners, cards and fouls' is verified only for corners. Cancelled or rescheduled-beyond-48-hours matches follow the generic fair-price rule (not shown in these corner texts).

rules_evidence.quote: Only corner kicks that are actually taken will count toward this market. Corner kicks that are awarded but not taken will not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The count is of taken corners; awarded corners that become goal kicks, are cancelled by VAR or not taken before a whistle do not count, so the data source must report taken rather than awarded.

rules_evidence.quote: combined record at least 9+ corners during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Extra-time corners count: in cup ties the exposure is up to 120 minutes, so knockout ties have a mean about 1.5-2.5 corners higher than the 90-minute version, whereas the 'taken' clause is absent from this series' sampled secondary text.

rules_evidence.quote: Barcelona records at least 6+ corners taken during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-corner thresholds are N+ for a single side, so the favourite's corner count depends on its territory and on whether it trails or leads, not on the match total alone.

rules_evidence.quote: Ipswich Town records at least 5+ corners taken during the entire game
rules_evidence.establishes: Underdog team thresholds (5+) are lower-mean events (about 4 corners) whose probability is driven by game state and set-piece pressure from the opponent's lead.

variants_and_edge_cases: Threshold construction: 'N+' with floor_strike N (greater_or_equal, e.g. 9+ total, 6+ team), a nested ladder of integer rungs; counts are discrete with mean about 10 total (sd 3-3.5) so adjacent rungs differ by 6-9 percentage points.
Extra time included in the corner count (per the entire-game wording), so cup knockouts and European two-leg matches with ET have longer exposure; league matches have no ET.
'Actually taken' language appears in EPL and La Liga series but not in the sampled UCL secondary text: the treatment of awarded-but-not-taken corners may differ by series and by data provider.
Cards and fouls have no live series here (the catalog's cards inputs have no contract to be verified against); referee-dependent card contracts, if listed, would need their own rules.
contract.settlement_data_source: Match data provider's corner-kick events (Opta-style events as used by Kalshi's sports data feed), counting corners taken in the entire game; the exact provider is not stated in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: A corner-count contract counts corner kicks taken over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time). Corners are a by-product of attacks that end blocked, deflected or parried: team expected corners scale with attacking volume and the share of attacks ending in blocked shots and crosses, and the opponent's defensive style (low block, clearance direction) multiplies it. Game state redistributes corners between the teams: the trailing side gains late, the leader concedes, so the favourite's team count depends on whether it scores early. Exposure (added time, VAR, extra time) and the 'taken versus awarded' definition adjust the count. Cards and fouls have no live contract in the ledger.

stages.name: Attacking pressure and territory
stages.description: Corners are generated when the attacking team's shots, crosses and passes are blocked or deflected over the byline, so each team's expected corners scale with its volume of attacks in the final third and the share of attacks that end in blocked shots; territorially dominant teams against deep blocks generate the highest counts, while transitional teams generate few.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) with mean about 5 per team; dispersion from variation in how attacks end.

stages.name: Opponent defending style
stages.description: A low block that blocks shots and crosses concedes many corners, a high line concedes few corners but more shots; the relevant measure is corners conceded per attack (block rate and clearance direction), not shots conceded; defenders' clearing habits and goalkeeper behaviour (tipping over the bar) are part of this.
stages.distribution: Team-level rate multiplier with sd about 15% across teams; interacts multiplicatively with the attacker's volume.

stages.name: Game state redistributes corners
stages.description: The trailing team pushes forward in the second half and wins more corners, while the leader defends deep and concedes them; late-game state generates 30-40% more corners for the trailer after the 60th minute. So the favourite's team corners are high only if it dominates without scoring early; an early lead lowers the favourite's count.
stages.distribution: Time-inhomogeneous intensity with score-state multipliers; negative association between early goals and the leader's subsequent corners.

stages.name: Match exposure: stoppage, VAR and extra time
stages.description: Exposure minutes (45+ each half, VAR delays, 30 minutes of ET in cups) scale the count; referees' added-time habits differ; a red card changes both teams' corner rates; and taken versus awarded definition removes a few percent of awarded corners.
stages.distribution: Exposure is a small discrete variable; ET adds expected 2-3 corners when played (about 30% of knockout ties).

stages.name: Rivalry, stakes and settlement
stages.description: High-stakes or derby matches increase tempo and aggression; settlement requires the count taken in the entire game from the match feed and mapping of N+ rungs; ladder consistency across rungs is a constraint.
stages.distribution: Mild shifts in mean (about +0.5 corners in derbies); deterministic settlement.

soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.label: Corners generated per attack by shot outcome (blocked, saved, deflected)
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.mechanism: Expected corners from the counts of blocked, saved-and-parried, and deflected attempts and crosses.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.rationale: Corners are a by-product of how attacks end; two teams with equal shots differ in corners according to the share of blocked shots and crosses; shot-based expected corners provide a more accurate estimate than past corner counts.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.measurement: For each team over the last 25 matches (half-life 12): corners per blocked shot, per saved shot, per cross attempted; expected corners = sum over expected shots by type for this match (opponent block rate and own shot-type mix) times coefficients; shrink coefficients to league with k=40 attempts; as-of previous matches.
soc.corner_generation_by_shot_outcome.why: Moves from historic corner counts to a causal expectation based on how attacks end.

soc.corner_state_multiplier.label: Score-state multipliers on corner rate by team role
soc.corner_state_multiplier.mechanism: Corner rate multiplier for the trailing and leading team by minute bucket and goal margin.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.rationale: Totals and team counts depend on when goals happen: an early goal by the favourite reduces its corners, a late equaliser chase increases the trailer's, so unconditional averages mis-state the favourite's team threshold.
soc.corner_state_multiplier.measurement: From event data with minute and score: corners per 10 minutes for trailing, level and leading states by pre-match favourite/underdog; estimate multiplier m_state relative to level state with Poisson regression, 8 seasons; shrink per team with k=300 minutes; combine with simulation of goal timing to get distribution of corners.
raw_data: corner events with minute and score state
soc.corner_state_multiplier.why: Provides the dynamic structure behind team-corner thresholds that static team averages cannot.

soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.label: Share of attacks through wide areas and crosses
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.mechanism: Crosses and wide-zone entries per 90 for the team and the opponent's concession of them.
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.rationale: Crossing teams generate blocked crosses and corners at much higher rates than central combination teams; the opponent's wide defending determines conversion.
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.measurement: Per team: crosses attempted per 90 and share of final-third entries via wide zones (last 25 matches, opponent-adjusted by regression with defence effects, shrink k=8 matches) and opponent's crosses conceded; the product (attack share × opponent concession relative to league mean) gives a matchup multiplier on expected corners.
soc.cross_and_wide_play_share.why: Captures matchup in how teams attack, which total corner counts depend on.

soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.label: Taken-versus-awarded and extra-time inclusion flags
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.mechanism: Per-series contract flags describing counting definition and the data provider's corner event type.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.rationale: Provider event definitions differ (awarded vs taken) and the sampled rules contain the 'actually taken' clause in some series only; wrong definition adds a systematic count error of a few percent.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.measurement: Parse rules into flags: taken_only, includes_ET, team vs combined; map provider field (e.g. corner taken event); measure the ratio taken/awarded in a historical sample from a provider with both (about 0.97-1.0) per league; store with version hash and timestamp.
soc.corner_taken_definition_flag.why: Settlement-definition input needed to label training data consistently.

soc.corners.reason: Opponent-adjusted corners for/against is the core rate; should be built from shot outcomes and state, not raw averages.

soc.fouls_cards.reason: Fouls and cards are not corner determinants and no live cards contract exists in the ledger; irrelevant to corner counts.

soc.referee.reason: Referee influence on corner counts is minor (via stoppages); card tendencies are irrelevant here.

soc.pace_press.reason: Possession and territory proxy volume; partially overlapping with corner rates.

soc.formation.reason: Formation determines width and crossing volume; hard to measure pregame.

soc.rivalry_intensity.reason: Derby effect on corner counts is small and not established; weak flag.

soc.stakes_leverage.reason: Stakes shift corner counts only marginally; mostly redundant with tempo.

soc.score_state.reason: Score-state response is the largest variation source but is not pregame; used to estimate state multipliers.

soc.set_piece_matchup.reason: Set-piece strength concerns conversion of corners into goals, not counts of corners; some link via aerial approach.

soc.var_intervention_rate.reason: VAR reviews lengthen stoppage and cancel some awarded corners; a small exposure effect.

soc.added_time.reason: Added minutes scale exposure; ET inclusion for cup matches matters more.

interactions.mechanism: A favourite's team corners depend on whether it scores early: an early goal drops its expected count while the underdog's rises, so the favourite's team-corner threshold has a negative interaction with goal timing; the match total changes less.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare favourite corner counts split by whether it scored before minute 30.

interactions.mechanism: A wide-attacking team facing a low block that clears crosses over the byline yields a multiplicative boost to corners: width volume times opponent concession rate, not their sum.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit corners on product of attack width and opponent concession index.

interactions.mechanism: Corners rise with attack volume but saturate against very deep blocks where possession is high and shots are few; beyond a possession level teams increase corners with diminishing returns as shot quality, not volume, becomes the limit.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot corners vs shots volume by possession decile.

interactions.mechanism: In knockout ties that reach extra time, exposure rises by a third, shifting both the total and team counts across integer rungs; the effect is a threshold at ET occurrence and depends on whether ET counts.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute corners in ET vs regulation by minute for ties.

nonlinearities.shape: Negative-binomial overdispersion; variance about 1.2-1.4 times the mean
nonlinearities.why: Counts are overdispersed by game-state heterogeneity, so Poisson-based rung probabilities are too narrow at both tails.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by margin: +1 goal raises trailer, saturates beyond 2
nonlinearities.why: Corner multipliers grow when trailing by one and saturate at two goals as the trailing team gives up or the leader parks.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in cross volume
nonlinearities.why: More crosses add corners at a decreasing rate as defensive clearances become less likely to go over the byline.

contract.settlement_definition: Per-player binaries over the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods): 'Goalscorer' = records at least 1 goal (floor 0.5, greater), 'Assists' = at least 1 assist, 'Score or Assist' = a goal or an assist, 'First Goalscorer' = the player records the first goal (plus a 'No Goal' outcome), and the 'First Goal Win' combo = the named player scores the first non-own goal AND his team wins (including any officially recognized tiebreaking procedure). If a player is active but never enters the game the market settles to the (last) fair market price before game start rather than to No; once a player enters, settlement is on his goals/assists. For first-goalscorer, a goal scored before the player enters as a substitute also settles to fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is active but never enters the game, the market settles to the fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: A bench player who never plays is not a loss: the contract pays the pre-game fair price, so the effective probability is a mix of P(plays) times P(scores|plays) and a refund, which removes most of the benching risk for substitutes.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first qualifying goal is scored before the player enters the match as a substitute, the market will also settle to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: A substitute's first-goalscorer contract is voided at fair price if the first goal arrives before he enters, so the relevant probability is conditional on being on the pitch at the time of the first goal.

rules_evidence.quote: records at least 1 assist during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Assists count in extra time; for knockout games the exposure exceeds 90 minutes, and assist attribution follows the official data provider's definition (not shown).

rules_evidence.quote: The first qualifying goal is the first non-own goal scored by either team, including regulation, stoppage time and any extra time.
rules_evidence.establishes: In the combo contract own goals are skipped when finding the first goal, a different definition from sibling team-level first-goal markets that credit own goals to the beneficiary.

rules_evidence.quote: records a goal or assist during the entire game (regulation, stoppage and any extra time periods)
rules_evidence.establishes: Score-or-assist is a union event: P(goal or assist) = P(goal) + P(assist) - P(both), where both is a within-player correlation, and a player cannot assist his own goal.

variants_and_edge_cases: DNP/bench rule: unlike many sports props, a player who never enters settles to fair price (stated 'before game start' vs 'last fair market price before game start' in different series), so the market contains an embedded refund and pre-game liquidity matters; once a player enters for one minute the contract resolves on his actual output.

First goalscorer: the 'No Goal' outcome resolves YES when no player records the first goal; the treatment of an own goal as the first goal (is it 'a player recording the first goal'?) is not visible, and KXINTLFRIENDLYFGW skips own goals by definition.

Assist attribution depends on the data provider (Opta-style definitions: the final pass leading directly to a goal, counting deflected passes in some cases; set-piece assists and penalty-won are not assists); own goals have no assist; this determines assists and score-or-assist labels.

Strikes are N+ for count thresholds (floor 0.5 means at least one) with also 2+ goals/hat-trick style rungs possible; extra time is included, so cup matches add exposure; abandonment mid-match with goals scored is not described.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official match data feed event log (goals with scorer, assists, substitutions) by the league data provider used by Kalshi; own goals excluded for the combo, credited to the beneficiary team for team contracts.

mechanism.summary: A player goal or assist prop is a thinned, allocated team event. The player must be on the pitch (starter, substitute, or unused, where an unused player settles at fair price); given minutes, his probability is one minus exp(-lambda) with lambda equal to the team's expected goals in this fixture times his share of team chances times conversion, plus penalty duty; assists are the same logic through creation share and the set-piece taker role, bounded by team goals and the teammates' finishing; score-or-assist is a union with within-player dependence. First goalscorer is a competing-risk race for the first goal with a categorical allocation and substitution timing, and the combo adds the dependence between scoring first and winning. Extra time counts, and own-goal and fair-price rules vary by series.

stages.name: Availability and entry into the game
stages.description: Whether the named player starts, enters as a substitute, or does not play at all determines his minutes distribution: starters average 80-90 minutes, substitutes 15-30. Because DNP settles at fair price, the relevant quantity is the conditional output given he plays, weighted by when he enters (an early sub is almost a starter) and the late lineup information about starting status.
stages.distribution: Three-point mixture: starter (about 85 minutes), substitute (about 20 minutes), unused; substitution times right-skewed.

stages.name: Team goal volume in this fixture
stages.description: The player's team has an expected goal total set by its opponent-adjusted attack against this opponent's defence and keeper; a player's chance is a share of that, so the same striker has a 55% scoring chance in a 3.0-xG home game and 25% in a 0.9-xG away game. Tempo and game state influence the team's volume.
stages.distribution: Team goals as an overdispersed count; the player's count conditional on team count is binomial-like with allocation by share.

stages.name: Player's share and conversion
stages.description: Share of team shots and chances, shot quality (location, header vs foot), finishing relative to xG and role in set pieces and penalties determine the player's goal rate per 90; penalty duty adds about 0.1-0.2 goals per match with penalty probability, and set-piece aerial threats add a lumpy component. Finishing must be regressed.
stages.distribution: Per-90 rate with heavy shrinkage (finishing persistence about 20-30%); zero-heavy count (P(0)>55% for forwards).

stages.name: Assist and chance-creation structure
stages.description: Assists depend on the player's creation (key passes, crosses, set-piece delivery) and on the finishing of the teammates who receive the chances; the set-piece taker (corners and free kicks) holds a disproportionate share of assists; an assist requires a goal to be scored, so assist probability is bounded by team goals and the player's share of creation.
stages.distribution: Compound process: team goals times player's share of assist credit; assists are rarer than goals (about 0.08 per 90 for creators), with large provider-definition noise.

stages.name: First-goal race and combo structure
stages.description: First goalscorer is a joint event: the team scores first (a competing-risk race), the scorer is the specific player (a share of first-goal routes weighted toward set pieces and penalties early), and for substitutes he must be on the pitch. The combo 'scores first and team wins' adds the positive dependence between scoring first and winning (about 70% of first-goal teams win-or-draw).
stages.distribution: Competing-risk race then categorical allocation; P(no goal) about 8%; conditional dependence between first goal and result.

stages.name: Settlement mapping
stages.description: Settlement maps official event logs to each player-level contract with specific DNP/fair-price, extra-time and own-goal rules; labelling errors arise from treating a fair-price settlement as a loss and from using different first-goal definitions in the combo and the team-level market.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from event feed; ambiguity in provider definitions.

soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.label: Starter/substitute/DNP mixture and settlement-adjusted probability
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.mechanism: Probabilities of starting, entering as a substitute at each minute, and not playing, with the contract's fair-price rule applied.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.rationale: Because a DNP settles at the fair price and a pre-first-goal substitution voids first-goalscorer contracts, the effective probability must be computed as a conditional on playing; mixing in a DNP loss biases prices of bench players downward.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.measurement: p_start from a logistic model on prior 5 starts, minutes, injury flags and rest (calibrated), p_sub|bench from historical sub rates by position and score state; substitution minute distribution from league data (median about 65 for attackers); P(plays) = p_start + (1-p_start)*p_sub; effective price probability P_eff = P(goal|plays) with the refund rule; for first goalscorer also P(on pitch at first goal); as-of strictly lineup release.
soc.dnp_and_sub_entry_settlement.why: Embedded refund rule is peculiar to this contract and changes the correct probability for every non-starter.

soc.assist_set_piece_role.label: Assist share by set-piece delivery and open-play creation
soc.assist_set_piece_role.mechanism: Player's share of team assists and key passes split by route (set-piece delivery, crosses, through balls).
soc.assist_set_piece_role.rationale: Assists are concentrated in a few creators and in the corner/free-kick taker, whose assist rate per 90 is 2-3 times that of a typical midfielder; the provider's definition of assist also matters.
soc.assist_set_piece_role.measurement: Over the last 40 matches (half-life 20): assists, key passes and xA per 90 split by set-piece vs open play; set-piece taker flags (corners, free kicks) from event data; expected assists = team expected goals × share of team goals assisted (about 70%) × player's share of assists (shrunk to position mean with k=10 matches); adjust for teammates' finishing (xG-to-goal conversion of recipients).
raw_data: xA, key passes, set-piece taker by match
soc.assist_set_piece_role.why: Needed because assist props are driven by creators and set-piece takers, not by xG/90.

soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.label: First goalscorer allocation model with competing risks and sub timing
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.mechanism: Joint probability that the player's team scores first and that he is the scorer, including time-varying intensity and substitution.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.rationale: P(first goalscorer) = integral over time of team first-goal intensity × player's share of that team's goals at that time × P(on pitch at t), which is not equal to team probability × season goal share, especially for early set-piece takers and substitutes.
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.measurement: Combine first_goal_hazard per team with the player's share of team goals by minute bucket (open play, set piece, penalty) from last 40 matches (shrink k=10) and P(on pitch at t) from the substitution model; P_first = ∫ h_team(t)·S(t)·share_i(t)·P_on(t) dt; also P(no goal) from joint survival; Monte Carlo 20k per match; as-of lineup release.
raw_data: goal events with minute and scorer
soc.first_goalscorer_race_model.why: Provides coherent probabilities for the first-goal and first-goal-win contracts.

soc.player_xg.reason: Non-penalty xG/90 and xA/90 supply the player-level rate; must be combined with minutes and match-specific team volume.

soc.player_shot_share.reason: Share of team shots/SOT is the allocation variable that turns team volume into player probability.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Starter status at lineup release is the largest single determinant of player-prop probability.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes distribution multiplies every rate; for substitutes the entry minute matters.

soc.penalty_taker_status.reason: Designated penalty taker has a distinct discrete scoring route (penalty about 0.3 per match).

soc.penalty_rate.reason: Penalty awards rate by team and referee changes the taker's probability by a few points.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.reason: Team expected goals in this fixture set the scale to which player shares apply.

soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.reason: Opponent's concession by zone and attacker position gives matchup adjustment for the specific player.

soc.gk.reason: Opponent keeper effect is small relative to team defence strength and mostly shrinks away.

soc.finishing_regression.reason: Prevents over-weighting hot streaks; shrinkage constant is essential.

soc.rotation_index.reason: Predicts lineup changes before release, useful for early-day prices.

interactions.mechanism: The settlement refund means a substitute's contract price should reflect P(goal|plays) with minutes-weighted rate; a bench striker's value is not his per-90 rate times 20 minutes alone but conditional on game state at entry (chasing games produce more entries and more goals).
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted vs realised goals for substitutes split by score state at entry.

interactions.mechanism: Player goal probability is team expected goals times share of shots times conversion; for a striker the elasticity to team volume is about 1, so doubling team lambda roughly doubles his lambda, and probability is 1-exp(-lambda) saturating.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress player goals on team xG times share with log link.

interactions.mechanism: The taker's extra probability exists only if a penalty is awarded (probability about 0.25-0.3 per match, higher with referees and teams that win penalties); the effect is a discrete bump, conditional on the taker being on the pitch.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare taker scoring rate in matches with penalties vs without.

interactions.mechanism: For first goalscorer a substitute's chance is conditional on entering before the first goal, which depends on rotation and the timing of the first goal: if the first goal comes early, subs are excluded, so the fair-price void changes the effective denominators.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(on pitch at first goal) by role and minute distribution of first goals.

interactions.mechanism: Assist probability scales with team goals and with the set-piece taker's share; in a high-xG match the taker's chance grows roughly linearly while a non-taker's grows more slowly, so team volume interacts with role.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit assists on team xG interacted with set-piece-taker flag.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating 1-exp(-lambda) from team volume to player P(1+)
nonlinearities.why: Player goal probability saturates: a doubling of lambda from 0.3 to 0.6 raises P by about 0.15 rather than doubling.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in minutes with substitution at 60-70
nonlinearities.why: Expected goals are roughly linear in minutes but entry minute distribution is bimodal (starters vs substitutes), so mean minutes misprices both groups.

nonlinearities.shape: Shrinkage weight rising with shots
nonlinearities.why: Weight on realised finishing grows with the sample of shots, n/(n+k) with k around 100.

contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series maps to this archetype in the ledger, so there is no contract text to read. The catalog target is a player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to an N+ threshold over a match. Settlement details (which shots count, whether blocked shots and headers are included, whether penalties count in shots and saves, regulation-only versus entire game with extra time, the DNP/substitute rule, the data provider's definitions) cannot be stated and are recorded as unresolved rather than inferred from the neighbouring goal/assist props, whose texts do say 'entire game' with fair-price DNP settlement.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shot definition: provider counts differ on blocked shots (an Opta 'shot' includes blocked, a 'shot on target' excludes them), on headers and on penalties; a shots threshold of 3+ for a striker is a different event under each, so the data provider must be identified before any calibration.

Goalkeeper saves count only shots on target that did not become goals, so saves = shots on target faced minus goals conceded (and own-goal and penalty details), making the contract a function of the opponent's SOT volume and of the goals actually conceded; a 4-0 loss can still have 4 saves while a 1-0 win can have 6.

DNP/substitute handling, extra time inclusion and abandoned matches are unknown; if the family follows neighbouring goal/assist props it would be entire-game with fair-price settlement for non-participants, but that is an assumption.
The catalog lists both players and keepers in one archetype although their drivers differ (player share of team shots versus opponent volume), so any live series would probably need separate keys.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not verified; presumably an official data-feed event log (shots, shots on target, saves per player) from the league's data provider used by Kalshi.

mechanism.summary: A player shot count thins the team's shot volume: minutes on the pitch (starter, early substitution), the team's expected shots against this defence, the player's share by role and set-piece duty, and a score-state multiplier since trailing teams shoot more. Shots on target add an accuracy layer. A goalkeeper's saves are a difference: opponent shots on target minus goals conceded, so the count depends on opponent SOT volume, shot quality and the actual goals, and it is non-monotone in opponent quality. Definitions of shots and saves depend on the data provider, and no live series exists to fix settlement.

stages.name: Playing time and role
stages.description: A shot count scales with minutes on the pitch and with the player's role: central forwards and wide attackers take 2-4 shots per 90 while defenders take under one; starting status, expected minutes and whether the player is subbed off in a game that is decided shift the count; for a goalkeeper the role is binary (starter or not), which makes minutes almost deterministic.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated by non-participation; for outfield players minutes distribution right-skewed; keeper minutes nearly constant at 90.

stages.name: Team shot volume in the fixture
stages.description: The team's total shots in this match come from its opponent-adjusted attacking volume, tempo and game plan against this defence; strong teams against low blocks produce 18+ shots, while counter-attacking teams produce fewer but better ones; the player's expected shots are the team volume times his share of shots, and shots on target multiplies by accuracy.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial team counts with mean about 12 and sd 4; player counts thin the team count with a binomial-like allocation, giving heavy overdispersion.

stages.name: Game-state response of shot volume
stages.description: The trailing team shoots more and from lower-quality positions, while the leader's volume declines; in blowouts the winner's volume often falls late while the loser's rises. So the player's shot count depends on whether his team leads, and the keeper's saves depend on the trailing opponent's late volume, making the final count a function of the match's score path.
stages.distribution: Time-varying intensity with state multipliers of +20% to +40% for the trailer; joint distribution of goals and shots (negative correlation within team).

stages.name: Shot conversion to on-target and to goals (keeper side)
stages.description: Shots on target depend on shot quality and the shooter's accuracy; a keeper's saves are SOT faced minus goals conceded, so strong shot quality (high PSxG) turns SOT into goals rather than saves, and the keeper's own shot-stopping quality shifts saves by a few tenths per match. Penalties add a rare high-conversion event.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of shots into on-target (about 33%) and then into goals (about 30% of SOT); saves count has mean about 3 per keeper with sd 1.7.

stages.name: Formation, personnel matchups and settlement definitions
stages.description: Which opposing defenders and tactical system face the shooter (central or wide, high line or deep block) affects his shot opportunities; the settlement counts depend on the provider's definitions of shots, blocked shots and saves, on extra time inclusion and on the participation rule.
stages.distribution: Matchup multipliers about 0.8-1.25; definition ambiguity is a deterministic offset (blocked shots count or not).

soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.label: Player shot rate multiplier by team score state
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.mechanism: Multipliers on a player's shots per 90 when his team is trailing, level or leading.
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.rationale: Strikers on trailing teams shoot more, and role-dependent: a poacher's share rises when his team chases while a creator's rises less, so state-conditional rates are needed in addition to season averages.
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.measurement: From events: player shots per 90 in each state by minute bucket relative to level; Poisson regression with offset log(minutes) and player random effect, 4 seasons; shrink to position mean with k=400 minutes in-state; combine with pregame team win probability to compute expected state mixture of shots.
raw_data: shot events with minute, player, score state
soc.player_shot_volume_state_response.why: Allows a pregame forecast that reflects the favourite or underdog role of the player's team.

soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.label: Expected saves from opponent SOT and shot quality
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.mechanism: Expected saves = expected opponent SOT minus expected goals conceded, using shot quality.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.rationale: Keeper saves are a difference of two counts: high SOT volume with many easy shots gives many saves, while the same volume of high-quality shots gives goals, so two matches with equal SOT can differ by two saves.
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.measurement: E[saves] = E[SOT faced] - E[goals conceded]; E[SOT faced] = opponent expected shots × SOT rate (opponent-adjusted, last 25 matches, half-life 12); E[goals] = E[SOT] × mean(PSxG per SOT) × keeper adjustment (shrunk PSxG-GA/SOT with k=60 SOT); includes penalty probability; variance via compound negative binomial; as-of lineup release.
raw_data: team shots, SOT, goals conceded, PSxG
soc.keeper_saves_from_sot_and_psxg.why: Defines saves mechanistically so the keeper's contract is not treated as a simple rate.

soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.label: Provider shot, shot-on-target and save definition mapping
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.mechanism: Flags and conversion ratios between provider definitions of shots, on-target shots and saves.
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.rationale: Different providers count blocked shots, headers and penalties differently, changing shot counts by 10-20%; calibrating on a different definition than the settlement feed produces systematic bias.
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.measurement: For a sample of 200+ matches with two providers, estimate ratio r = shots_settlement / shots_training by player position, blocked-share and penalty treatment; store mapping per league; apply multiplicative correction and widen variance; version-hash the definitions.
raw_data: two-provider shot counts for same matches
soc.shot_event_definition_mapping.why: Label consistency is a prerequisite for calibration given no rules text exists.

soc.shots.reason: Team shots and SOT per 90, opponent- and state-adjusted, are the volume base for both player shots and keeper saves.

soc.player_shot_share.reason: Player's share of team shots and SOT is the allocation variable; must be split by open play, set pieces and penalties.

soc.lineups_pit.reason: Starter confirmation determines participation, the largest single factor for a player prop.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Minutes (start, early substitution) multiplies the shot rate.

soc.keeper_workload.reason: Expected SOT faced is the core of the saves model; must be reconciled with goals conceded.

soc.gk.reason: Keeper PSxG-GA matters little for saves counts compared with SOT volume; small shrunk effect.

soc.pace_press.reason: Tempo and pressing correlate with shot volume, partially redundant with team shots.

soc.score_state.reason: Not a pregame input; used to estimate state multipliers.

soc.opp_shot_profile_by_zone.reason: Defence concession by zone and attacker position matches the shooter's role.

soc.formation.reason: Tactical matchups are hard to measure pregame; weak evidence of incremental power for shots.

interactions.mechanism: A striker's expected shots are team volume times share times a state multiplier; an underdog's striker has a lower base volume but a large trailing-state boost, and the three factors multiply, so the expected count is not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit player shots with interaction of team win probability and role in a Poisson regression.

interactions.mechanism: Saves equal SOT minus goals, so they are non-monotone in shot quality: strong opponents give more SOT but also more goals, and saves peak at moderate quality and high volume, e.g. for a mid-strength opponent against a deep-block team.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare saves against SOT and PSxG deciles.

interactions.mechanism: Participation is a threshold: if a striker is not named in the XI, the prop's shot rate falls to a substitute's rate, producing a step change; announcements at about T-60 minutes are the information event.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast shot rates for starters and unused players and measure price jump.

interactions.mechanism: A winger's shots depend on the opposing full-back and the system: against a back five the wide player takes fewer shots and more crosses, so the matchup effect is conditional on the opponent's formation.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact shot rate with opposing formation indicator by position.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-monotone in opponent shot quality
nonlinearities.why: Saves are SOT minus goals; as quality rises, goals take share from saves, so saves peak at intermediate quality and decline.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in the goal deficit
nonlinearities.why: Trailing by one lifts shots about 20-30% but trailing by three adds little since players shoot from low-quality positions with fatigue.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in entry minute for substitutes
nonlinearities.why: Shot count is near-linear in minutes for starters but a substitute entering after 75 minutes has a sharply smaller expected count.
